warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283-L286


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`schnibblesTotal` will be significantly lowered, reducing rewards for users.

## Proof of Concept
The current math used for farming schnibbles (inside [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283-L286))  has a `finalBonus` that will be applied to `schnibblesTotal`, however the calculation incorrectly encloses the total amount before the division:

$$
\frac{schnibblesTotal + schnibblesTotal \cdot finalBonus}{100}
$$

Where the real bonus calculation should be:

$$
schnibblesTotal + \left( \frac{schnibblesTotal \cdot finalBonus}{100} \right)
$$


This in tern will transform the bonus calculation into a penalty one. Bellow is the [code snippet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283-L286) where that takes place.

```solidity
// (schnibblesTotal + schnibblesTotal * finalBonus) / 100 
schnibblesTotal = uint256((int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100);
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change the formula:

```diff
    // (schnibblesTotal + schnibblesTotal * finalBonus) / 100 
-   schnibblesTotal = uint256((int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100);

    // schnibblesTotal + (schnibblesTotal * finalBonus / 100)
+   schnibblesTotal = uint256(int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus / 100));
```


## Assessed type

Math

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L287-L293


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Not farming the plot while updating the landlord fee will cause a portion of the time with the new fee to be charged by the old one.

## Proof of Concept
[updateTaxRate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L92-L101) does not farm the plots that it is used in, meaning they still keep the old value inside `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`.

When farming them [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L287-L293) will always use the old tax to calculate the current `schnibblesLandlord` tax and then update the tax to the latest one.

```solidity
   schnibblesLandlord = (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate) / 1e18;

   toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate = timestamp;
   toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord].currentTaxRate;
```

This will cause the tax to be outdated. Users can use this accidentally or maliciously to pay lower tax (or higher):

1. At T1 tax is 10% and our user farms the plot.
2. At T2 the landlord changes the tax to 20%
3. At T3 our user farms the plot again, only paying 10% tax for the time T1 to T3.

In the example above our user paid the old tax for T2-T3, although the landlord had updated it.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Farming all of the plots when the tax is changed may be too hard, however a formula can be made that will calculate the weight of old and new tax depending on the time it was changed. 

An example is if tax is 10% for 1 day and 20% for 1 day, then when the total tax collected for the 2 days would be 15%.


## Assessed type

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L92


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Not updating the time will cause [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) to farm more rewards to users than they should.

## Proof of Concept
[updateTaxRate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L92-L101) doesn't update `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`. This cna be considered an issue as it breaks the implementation inside [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) made to calculate the new rewards based on `lastUpdated` if the plot is dirty.

```solidity
   if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
       timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
       toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
   }
   ...
   schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

Since the above concept is implemented inside [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261), it's intentions are clearly to use the last tax updated timestamp --`plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` -- as timestamp when the `toilerState` is marked as `dirty`.

However that won't be the case as multiple tax chnages can be made without updating `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Update the `lastUpdated` time inside [updateTaxRate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L98C9-L99):

```diff
    uint256 oldTaxRate = plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate;
    plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate = newTaxRate;
+   plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated = block.timestamp;
```


## Assessed type

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Pausable unstake/withdraws can be dangerous as they restrict users in the case of an emergency, like a hack - when withdraws are most needed.

## Proof of Concept
[unstakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175) is pausable:

```solidity
    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
```

However having pausability on critical user functions like unstake is dangerous as it can lead to pretty bad scenarios in the cases of a hack. Needing to unpause the whole system in order for users to withdraw will enable the hacker to exploit it even more.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Removed the `notPaused` modifier.

```diff
-    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
+    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) {
```

Another solution is to make 2 pause mods, normal - pausing everything but unstake, and emergency - pausing the whole system.


## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344-L346
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Price updates can be triggered for different contracts with less (2) than the required threshold (3).

Change in the price will also change the weight on **each** landlord, as [_getNumPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344-L346) relies on LockManager's weight, which in tern is [quantity * price](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L481-L491).

## Proof of Concept
When a new price for contracts is requested with [proposeUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142) it needs to pass a threshold (currently 3) of approvals or disapproval in order to be accepted or deleted.

However currently the only validation, inside [approveUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177) or [disapproveUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L212), that is done is on the price, missing a check if the proposed contracts are the same as the ones that are approved:

```solidity
    function approveUSDPrice(uint256 _price) external
        onlyOneOfRoles([Role.PriceFeed_1, Role.PriceFeed_2, Role.PriceFeed_3, Role.PriceFeed_4, Role.PriceFeed_5])
    {
        ...
        if (usdUpdateProposal.proposedPrice != _price) {
            revert ProposalPriceNotMatchedError();
        }
```

This would allow a corrupt oracle to front-run an approval with [disapproveUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L212), followed by [proposeUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142) and make the approval for another set of contracts.

Example:
1. Price X is proposed for contracts 1,2,3.
2. 1 oracle votes for approval and 2 for disapproval.
3. Another oracle votes for approval.
4. However a front-run:
- calls [disapproveUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L212) to remove the current vote
- calls [proposeUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142) on the same price - X, bit for contracts 4,5,6
5. The original approval for contracts 1,2,3 is now an approval for contract 4,5,6

The attacker has gained 1 extra vote for, making him 2/5, requiring one more in order to capture the proposal.


---


The above would enable anyone controlling 2/5 price feeds to control the prices.
Changing the threshold to 2 will make any singe price feed have control over the prices.

**This is breaking the core invariant of requiring 3 price feeds (majority) to agree on the same rice for the same contracts.**

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use an ID for each proposal that will encode the `price` and `_contracts`. This will make each proposal different from the last.


## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can capture rewards even when their plots are `dirty`.

## Proof of Concept
1. [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) has the ability to make a plot `dirty` if the current landlord available plots are smaller than the ID of this plot:

```solidity
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

When a plot is made dirty it's rewards are claimed for the last time, and it becomes basically useless. The only way to remove the `dirty` tag is to unstake and stake the NFT again. That implies that if a plot gets `dirty` even once, it's rewards are stopped. 

2. The number of available plots is calculates inside [_getNumPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344-L346) and it represents the weight of our user divided by the price per plot:
```solidity
    function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
        // weight / price
        return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    }
```
Where weight is calculated inside [getLockedWeightedValue](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L481-L491), as `quantity * price`:

```solidity
lockedWeighted += (
   deltaDecimal 
   * lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity
   * configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].usdPrice) 
   / 1e18;
```

3. And finally the `price` can be changed by oracle providers using [proposeUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142).

---

When we take the above points into account we can see that a change in price can cause a change in available plots, which in tern my make some plots dirty.

However users can avoid such changes, by waiting them out and claiming the rewards for the whole period, even the time when their plot should have been considered `dirty`.

Example:
- Plot price is 100 weight, where each asset is priced as 1.
1. At T1 user has 200 weight and 2 plots.
2. At T2 price changes from 1 to 0.95, making his weight 195 and causing his plot to become dirty **if farmed**.
3. At T3 price goes up again to 1.
4. User farms his plot capturing rewards for T1 to T3, even thought his plot would have been dirty from T2 to T3.

In the above case our user captured rewards for a time where his plot should have been dirty. 

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Given the current implementation I cannot provide a simple solution to this issue. My best suggestion is to enable anyone to farm plots inside the LandManager, but that may cause issues in other parts of the code. Another solution can be to introduce PVP in the form of liquidations, rewarding users who punish dirty plots.


## Assessed type

Oracle

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When a plot can be marked as `dirty` it will pay rewards only from `toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate` up to `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`, which may mean, that rewards are not paid up to the current `block.timestamp`.

However users can update their own metadata and claim for their `dirty` plot up to `block.timestamp`

## Proof of Concept
If a plot is to be marked as `dirty` [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) will claim the rewards only up to `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`, which can be in the past.


```solidity
    if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
        timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
        toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
    }

    ...

    schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

However users can prevent that and claim their rewards for their dirty plots by updating their landlord's `plotMetadata` using [updatePlotMetadata](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L124-L126). That can be done by locking some amount (can be 1 wei) for their landlord with [LockManager::lockOnBehalf](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L278-L294), which will trigger [AccountManager::forceHarvest](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L151-L155), setting their `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` to the current `block.timestamp`.

Example:
1. At T1 our user stakes at the last free slot of a landlord.
2. At T2 the landlord withdraws some of his locked tokens, decreasing his active plots.
3. At T3 our user, who's plot is less than the active plots (will be `dirty` after harvest), wants to claim his rewards.
4. He calls [lockOnBehalf](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L278-L294) for the landlord, locking 1 wei and updating his metadata.
5. Then he claims his rewards, claiming from T1 to T3.

Notice how our user has claimed rewards for time that his plot would have been considered `dirty` (T2-T3) and not paid rewards.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
A really good solution would be to make a landlord specific map that will track the time at which plots become `dirty` and when [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) is invoked it will only query that plot and see if it's dirty or not. Example code:

```solidity
   if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
      timestamp = plotDirtyTime[_toiler.plotId];
      toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
      plotDirtyTime[_toiler.plotId] = 0;
   }
```
The only downside to this would be that on [LockManager::unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L407) we would need to iterate over the array and set the removed plots to the current `block.timestamp`. That may also cause an issue if we unlock for more than 500 or 1000 plots as the gas would get expensive.


## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can be DOS from using staking or unstaking all of their NFTs.

## Proof of Concept
1. [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232) is triggered in all of the main functions - [transferToUnoccupiedPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L202), [unstakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175) and [stakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L135). If that function reverts those will revert too.

2. If a user triggers [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261) and his `plotId` is bigger than the available plots, his `timestamp` (for reward math) will get set to `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`.

```solidity
   if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
       timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
       toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
   }

   ...

   //@audit but what if _toiler.lastToilDate > timestamp ? 
   schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

3. [_getNumPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344-L346) calculates the available plots using - `weight / price` formula, where the weight is calculated inside [getLockedWeightedValue](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L481-L491) to be - `quantity * price / 1e18`.
- `quantity` is the amount of tokens the landlord deposits.
- `price` is a custom price variable that is updated by oracles.


---


With the above 3 an issue can appear, where `_toiler.lastToilDate` is bigger than `timestamp`, leading to an underflow and a revert. This will cause a completed DOS for every user that has a plot, considered as dirty. This can happen with price updates, lowering the landlord's weight, causing his plots to decrease.

Example:
1. Landlord has 500 tokens, valued at 1 each, with 100 for a single plot - 5 plots total
2. User1 stakes 1 of his 10 NFTs to this landlord's last plot.
3. Oracles update the price with [proposeUSDPrice](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142) from 1 to 0.995 (0.5% decrease), causing the landlord's weight to decrease to 497,5, marking his last plot as dirty.
4. Our user tries to unstake to be no longer on a `dirty` plot, however the TX fails as `_toiler.lastToilDate > plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`, causing [timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L281) to underflow.
5. His 9 other NFTs are also stuck as [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232) harvest for all 10 of them at the same time.

Now there are 2 solutions for this DOS to stop
1. The landlord update his metadata with [updatePlotMetadata](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L116-L129), by locking some tokens - not user dependent, he can do it if he wants to.
2. There is a bug, described in another of my issues, where the user can lock for the landlord and update his metadata - the user relaying on a bug/another procedure to unlock his tokens.

Notice how the only solutions to this DOS are a bug/another procedure and for the user to wait on other entities.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
With the current implementation I am unaware of how this can be fixed. My suggestion is to redo the reward math and think of other ways to lower rewards for dirty plots.


## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L299


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
[_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L299) sets `lastPetMunchable` to `timestamp` (where that time is in the past), which will enable the landlord to [SnuggeryManager::pet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/SnuggeryManager.sol#L232-L233) multiple times in a row, gaming the petting reward system.

## Proof of Concept
Farming a `dirty` plot with [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L299) will set the landlord's `lastPetMunchable` to his `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`, which can (and most likely will) be in the past:

```solidity
   if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
      timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
      toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
   }

   landlordMetadata.lastPetMunchable = uint32(timestamp);
```

This variable is used inside [SnuggeryManager::pet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/SnuggeryManager.sol#L232-L233) as a check to prevent users from petting a lot of NFTs in 1 TX. More specifically, it allows users to pet 1 NFT every 10 minutes.

```solidity
        if (_petterPlayer.lastPetMunchable + 10 minutes > block.timestamp) {
            revert PetTooSoonError();
        }
```

However thanks to [_farmPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L299) a landlord can pet multiple times in a single block (even a single TX):

Set up at T1:
- Have a few different accounts that each have staked 1 NFT per plot.
- [unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L407) all of his assets, setting `lastUpdated` to T1, and having 0 free plots.

Attack at T1+10:
1. pet an NFT at T1+10 min and earn a reward
2. Farm 1 dirty plot, from one of his accounts, setting his `lastPetMunchable` to T1
3. pet another NFT
4. Farm another, again setting `lastPetMunchable` to T1
5. pet another NFT
...

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Set `landlordMetadata.lastPetMunchable` to `block.timestamp` instead of `timestamp`:

Same can be said for the rest of previously mentioned variables.

Manual review

Take into account such behavior when changing these variables.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `_getNumPlots` function in the Munchables `LandManager` contract is used to get the plots of land a landlord owns using the formula `_getNumPlots = lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;` due to rounding down in solidity this disfavors landlords and disincentivizes land ownership.


## Proof of Concept
the `getLockedWeightedValue` in the above formula "Calculates the USD value of all tokens locked by a player, weighted by their yield" and is used at several locations in the codebase

Consider the following case, Landlord locks Tokens worth 30USD(plus yield) in the `LockManager`, and the price per_plot is 30USD , in this case, according to `_getNumPlots` landlord has 1 plot of land, any even the most minuscle fluctuation in value of locked tokens to 29.99USD now means the landlord has 0 land allocated, even when the same number of token is still locked.
In solidity 
_getNumPlots = 29/30 = 0 plots of land

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Protocol should round in favor of `landlords` to incentivize land ownership, small fluctuations in price should not change the status quo.

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L145-L146


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The incorrect plot range check can cause transactions to fail due to a wrongly implemented validation, while we have both the plot and the NFT. This disrupts the staking process, leading to losing the opportunity for both parties, staker and landlord.

## Proof of Concept

The issue lies in the incorrect validation of the plot range, which can cause transactions to fail even when both the plot and the NFT are available.

```solidity
uint256 totalPlotsAvail = _getNumPlots(landlord);
if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```
```solidity
function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
   return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
}
```
The current validation uses >=, which incorrectly allows for the possibility of staking to an invalid plot index.
This results in a transaction failure despite having both the plot and the NFT available.

**Example scenario:**

Let's consider a scenario where the landlord has exactly one plot. This means totalPlotsAvail will be 1.

Landlord: Has only one plot.
Staker: Attempts to stake an NFT to plotId 1.

This scenario will lead to a failed transaction, causing the staking process to be disrupted. Both the staker and the landlord lose the opportunity to:

1. Earn Points: The staking process is tied to farming points or other incentives. By failing to stake, both parties miss out on potential rewards and benefits.
2. Utilize Assets: Despite having the necessary plot and NFT, the faulty validation prevents their proper use, leading to frustration and inefficiency.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

By correcting the condition to use >, we ensure the plot index is correctly validated:
```solidity
if (plotId > totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```



## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L271


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

In `LandManager::_reconfigure` the state variables are set. REALM_BONUSES is set the following way:
        
```solidity
    REALM_BONUSES = configStorage.getSmallIntArray(StorageKey.RealmBonuses);
```

Which may result in setting negative numbers as REALM_BONUSES may have its values set as negative.

Later on, whenever `LandManager::_farmPlots(address)` is used the logic inside it uses the values of the REALM_BONUSES based on index:

```solidity
finalBonus =
                int16(
                    REALM_BONUSES[
                        (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
                            uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
                    ]
                ) +
                int16(
                    int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
                );
```

As a result if one of the values inside REALM_BONUSES is negative and the index happens to be the one in which the REALM_BONUSES stores the negative value, this will cause the inaccuracy.

The `finalBonus` variable inside the `LandManager::_farmPlots(address)` is used for multiplication and causing the `schnibblesTotal` to be inaccurate too which is used for multiplication and substraction and so forth.

## Proof of Concept
1. Deploy and initialize 'LandManager' contract
2. Configure initial tax rates by calling relevant functions as usual
3. Call `LandManager::stakeMunchables` (has a forceFarmPlots modifier) with valid data or directly `LandManager::_farmPlots`

## Tools Used
Solidity

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make REALM_BONUSES of type `uint16[]` instead of `int16[]` and thus update in `LandManager::_reconfigure` 
```solidity
+    REALM_BONUSES = configStorage.getSmallUintArray(StorageKey.RealmBonuses);
-    REALM_BONUSES = configStorage.getSmallIntArray(StorageKey.RealmBonuses);
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L318


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In `LandManager::_removeTokenIdFromStakedList` every single time the function is called we iterate through the whole `munchablesStaked` in order to:
1. Check that there is a tokenId with such tokenId
2. If there is one then to remove it.

Provided that a lot of users stake munchables the array inside the map `munchablesStaked` will become way to gas expensive to iterate through causing self DOS.

High - too many staked munchables result in extremely high gas consumption making `_removeTokenIdFromStakedList` unusable and not be able to remove tokenIds from staked list

## Proof of Concept
1. Deploy and initialize `LandManager` contract
2. Configure initial tax rates by calling relevant functions as usual
3. Large amount of munchables are staked
4. Call `LandManager::_removeTokenIdFromStakedList` with any valid params

## Tools Used
Solidity

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use another map to store the tokenIds to address. Thus, you will NOT have to iterate through the whole list just to check whether there is such a tokenId to be removed and saving massively from gas:

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L27

```solidity
+     mapping(uint256 => address) munchablesTokenIdsToAddress;
-     mapping(address => uint256[]) munchablesStaked;
```

Another alternative is to have a map which stores the tokenIds indexs by ranges and iterating only a specific range (batches) instead of the whole map. However, this adds additional complexity, because each time a token is added/removed you have to update the other map as well and make sure you set the correct ranges.

Overall, the first solution above is one of the best.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L259
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L281
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L163


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The user can lock his NFT and be unable to unstake it causing him the loss of his NFT and also the loss of `schnibbles`.

## Proof of Concept
Imagine this scenario: 
1. Alice has staked ETH in the protocol , which means she has certain amount of plots, calculated by `_getNumPlots` function:
```
    function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
        return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    }
```
2. Bob decides to stake his munchable NFT with the `stakeMunchable` function with landlord parameter `Alice` and plotId 0 or plotId 1, assuming Alice has enough staked to have plots.
3. Now Alice at no point in time updates her Plot metadata leaving the `lastUpdated` variable in the PlotMetadata to it's default value of 0.
4. Alice decides to unstake her tokens in the protocol, leaving her with close to 0 or funds under the `PRICE_PER_PLOT` variable , resulting in `_getNumPlots` function returning 0
5. Bob decides to unstake his munchable  NFT and `_farmPlots` function is called.
We get to this check that will be triggered because Alice has no staked funds and `_getNumPlots` returns 0:
```
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) { //! What happens when a landlord removes his staked tokens?
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated; //!lastUpdated can it be 0?
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```
`timestamp` is seto to  'lastUpdated' variable but remember this variable is 0 because Alice never updated her Plot metadata, look at point 3 above.
So timestamp being set to 0 we get to this calculation:
```
    schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```
Where `timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate` will be 0 - timestamp of NFT staking. 
This will return <0 and cause the function to revert.
6. Since the `_farmPlots` function reverts and it's called basically everywhere including in the `unstakeMunchable` and `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` this will leave the NFT stuck in the contract.

## Tools Used
Manual review
Integrate a check for the `lastUpdated` parameter for Plot metadata in the `_farmPlots` function.





## Assessed type

ERC721

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L292
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L166


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Landlord can loose on potential profits and get incentivized to participate.

## Proof of Concept
Imagine this scenario.
1. Bob stakes some collateral and get's a number of plots based on the amount in USD of his collateral calculated in `_getNumPlots`.

2. Alice decides to stake her munchables in Bob's plot.

3. Let's say Bob has 5 plots and Alice stakes in all of Bob's plots.
Toiler state gets updated:
```
....
        toilerState[tokenId] = ToilerState({
            lastToilDate: block.timestamp,
            plotId: plotId,
            landlord: landlord,
            latestTaxRate: plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate, //! what happens if I increase taxRate suddenly?
            dirty: false
        });
....
```
So the `latestTaxRate` is the `currentTaxRate` which can be the default value if Bob never used the `updateTaxRate` function to update the tax rate.

4. Bob decides to update his tax rate so that he can get better return of investment. Calls the `updateTaxRate` and makes his tax rate bigger/close to max.
Now the plots are still occupied with Alice's munchables, but the `_farmPlots` function uses the old `_toiler.latestTaxRate` to calculate `schnibblesLandlord` and AFTER that updates `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`:
```
...
            schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
            schnibblesTotal = uint256((int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100);
            schnibblesLandlord = (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate) / 1e18;

            toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate = timestamp;
            toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord].currentTaxRate;
...
```
This means that if the staker (Alice) never usntakes or moves her munchables to another plot the `_farmPlots` function will not trigger and update the new tax rate that Bob set. Meaning Bob cannot impose his new tax rate willingly.

5. Even if Bob unstakes his collateral and stake it again, he still won't be able to impose his new tax rate.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Update in tax rate `updateTaxRate` should properly implement change in `latestTaxRate` of `toilerState`.

title: Unsafe cast from int256 to uint256 in `LandManager._farmPlots(...)` will overflow
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In `LandManager::_farmPlots(...)`, `schnibblesTotal` is repeatedly being typecasted to `int256` to be multiplied by `finalBonus` as such:

```solidity
finalBonus =
    int16(
        REALM_BONUSES[
            (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
                uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
        ]
    ) +
    int16(
        int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
    );
schnibblesTotal =
    (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
    BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
schnibblesTotal = uint256(
    (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
        (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
);
```

However, if `finalBonus` is negative, then `int256(schnibblesTotal) +(int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus))` will be negative, and casting it to `uint256` directly will cause `schnibblesTotal` to overflow into a huge value. This will cause `_farmPlots(...)` to always revert whenever it is called, making it impossible for the user to work with his NFT collection in the `LandManager` contract, as every function calls `_farmPlots(...)`.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L270
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283

As NFT attributes are randomly generated, the following test scenario takes values for the REALM_BONUSES and RARITY_BONUSES as seen in the provided [deployment constants](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/deployments/utils/consts.ts#L129)

1. Naruto has a collection of munchables, and wants to stake some of them into Sasuke's plots, where Sasuke's snuggery is in the `Drench` realm.

2. Naruto initially stakes a munchable from the `Everfrost` realm with a `Common` rarity.

3. The `stakeMunchable(...)` call will succeed because `_farmPlots(...)` will not go through any stakes, because Naruto does not have any staked munchables and `munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length = 0`.

4. After some time, Naruto wants to get his munchable NFT back and tries to unstake from Sasuke's plots.

5. This time the logic in `_farmPlots(...)` will be initiated.

6. From the realm and rarity bonuses of Naruto's staked munchable, the `finalBonus` will be:

```solidity
finalBonus = int16(REALM_BONUSES[(uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) + uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)]) + int16(int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)]));

finalBonus = int16(REALM_BONUSES[uint256(0)*5 + uint256(1)]) + int16(int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(1)]));

finalBonus = int16(-10) + int16(0) // REALM_BONUSES[1] = -10, RARITY_BONUSES[1] = 0

finalBonus = -10
```

7. Let's presume that `schnibblesTotal` is something like `10e18`.
8. With these values we can now observe the following overflow:

```bash
➜ uint256 schnibblesTotal = 10e18;
➜ int256 finalBonus = -10;
➜ schnibblesTotal = uint256((int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100);
➜ schnibblesTotal
Type: uint256
├ Hex: 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff3828ec4b6260000
├ Hex (full word): 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff3828ec4b6260000
└ Decimal: 115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039456684007913129639936
```
9. Afterwards `schnibblesTotal` is further multiplied, which will lead to EVM reverts, making it impossible for Naruto to get his NFT back, or even stake new NFT's as `_farmPlots(...)` will always go through the above-described overflow.

NB: I also contacted the sponsors to confirm that the `finalBonus` can be negative and [they confirmed it](https://gist.github.com/Welith/ea2793529f7d62d241ecbcb89b3e2249).



## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

The mitigation here may not be straightforward, as the easiest solution is to add a `-` sign to the `int256` value if it is negative, before casting it to `uint256`.

```solidity
diff --git a/src/managers/LandManager.sol b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
index 4da770a..10ab9fb 100644
--- a/src/managers/LandManager.sol
+++ b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
@@ -280,10 +280,13 @@ contract LandManager is BaseBlastManagerUpgradeable, ILandManager {
             schnibblesTotal =
                 (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                 BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
-            schnibblesTotal = uint256(
-                (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
-                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
-            );
+            int256 potentialSchnibbles = (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
+                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100;
+            if (potentialSchnibbles < 0) {
+                schnibblesTotal = uint256(-potentialSchnibbles);
+            } else {
+                schnibblesTotal = uint256(potentialSchnibbles);
+            }
```

Another solution could be to set `schnibblesTotal` to `0` if `finalBonus < 0`, so that no `schnibbles` are awarded for the NFT, but this will make it unfavorable for the user to stake this specific NFT.

```diff
diff --git a/src/managers/LandManager.sol b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
index 4da770a..810a831 100644
--- a/src/managers/LandManager.sol
+++ b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
@@ -280,10 +280,13 @@ contract LandManager is BaseBlastManagerUpgradeable, ILandManager {
             schnibblesTotal =
                 (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                 BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
-            schnibblesTotal = uint256(
-                (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
-                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
-            );
+            int256 potentialSchnibbles = (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
+                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100;
+            if (potentialSchnibbles < 0) {
+                schnibblesTotal = 0;
+            } else {
+                schnibblesTotal = uint256(potentialSchnibbles);
+            }
```

All in all, the core logic for a negative `finalBonus` should be revised so that it best suits the protocol needs.














## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L272
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L278


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `LandManager::_farmPlots(...)` can potentially revert due to `Index out of bounds` error, if the global `REALM_BONUSES` or `RARITY_BONUSES` arrays are not properly set.

## Proof of Concept
The `LandManager.sol` contract allows users to stake their munchables to other users' plots, in order to farm schnibbles. The schnibble rewards are increased with a bonus, which is formed from various user and NFT attributes. The calculation of this bonus is based on the `REALM_BONUSES` and `RARITY_BONUSES` arrays, which are set prior to deployment:

```solidity
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
       __SNIP
    finalBonus =
        int16(
@>            REALM_BONUSES[
                (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
                    uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
            ]
        ) +
        int16(
@>            int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
        );
    __SNIP__
}
```

If the values in these arrays are misconfiguted, then the current calculation for the indexes will fail for specific realm and rarity combinations, leading to `_farmPlots()` to always revert, blocking all functionalities in the `LandManager` contract. This has been properly handled in the [BonusManager::getFeedBonus(...)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/BonusManager.sol#L102-L112) function, meaning that the dev elopment team are aware of such a problem.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Use the same index checks as done in the [BonusManager::getFeedBonus(...)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/BonusManager.sol#L102-L112) function, but instead of reverting set a default value.

```diff
+++ b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
@@ -267,15 +267,17 @@ contract LandManager is BaseBlastManagerUpgradeable, ILandManager {
             immutableAttributes = nftAttributesManager.getImmutableAttributes(
                 tokenId
             );
+            uint256 realmIndex = (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
+                uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm);
+            if (realmIndex >= REALM_BONUSES.length)
+                realmIndex = DEFAULT_REALM_BONUS_INDEX;
+            uint256 rarityIndex = uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity);
+            if (rarityIndex >= RARITY_BONUSES.length)
+                rarityIndex = DEFAULT_RARITY_BONUS_INDEX;
             finalBonus =
+                int16(REALM_BONUSES[realmIndex]) +
                 int16(
-                    REALM_BONUSES[
-                        (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
-                            uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
-                    ]
-                ) +
-                int16(
-                    int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
+                    int8(RARITY_BONUSES[rarityIndex])
                 );
             schnibblesTotal =
                 (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
```

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232-L310


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `_farmPlots` function contains an unbounded loop that iterates over all staked Munchables for a given user.If a user has a large number of staked Munchables, the function may exceed the block gas limit, causing the transaction to fail.Also an attacker could potentially stake a large number of Munchables to make the `_farmPlots` function unusable, effectively denying service to themselves and also potentially affecting other contract functionalities that rely on this function.




## Proof of Concept
Looking at the loop in the [`_farmPlots`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232-L310) function:

```solidity
for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
    // Loop body with multiple operations and state changes
}
```

This loop iterates over all staked Munchables, performing multiple operations for each, including external calls and state changes. The gas cost increases with the number of staked Munchables, potentially exceeding the block gas limit.

## Tools Used
Manual code review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Allow farming a specified number of Munchables per transaction. This would enable users to farm their plots in multiple transactions if needed. Also, you can implement a check within the loop to break if the remaining gas is low:

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L213-L222


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
1. Inconsistent State:
The toilerState mapping will have an outdated plotId, 
leading to incorrect tracking of the staked NFT's location.

2. Reward Calculation Errors:
Functions that rely on the plotId in toilerState for calculating rewards 
or other plot-specific logic will produce incorrect results.

For example, 
the following line inside the `_farmPlots` function 
reads the wrong plotId
```
if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) 
```

3. Data Integrity Issues:
The contract's overall data integrity is compromised, 
which might cause unexpected behaviors in other functions or integrations.
 

## Proof of Concept

The `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` function in the `LandManager` contract allows users 
to transfer a staked munchable NFT from one plot to another unoccupied plot. 

However, the current implementation does not update the plotId 
in the `toilerState` mapping.

Example Scenario


1. Initial State: The NFT with tokenId 1234 is staked in plotId 1.


```
toilerState[1234] = ToilerState({
    lastToilDate: 1627593600,  // Timestamp
    plotId: 1,                 // Initially staked in plotId 1
    landlord: 0x123...,        // Address of the landlord
    latestTaxRate: 500,        // Example tax rate
    dirty: false               // Dirty flag
});
```
2. Function Call: We transfer the NFT to a new plotId 2.
Call the transferToUnoccupiedPlot function
```
landManager.transferToUnoccupiedPlot(1234, 2);
```

3. Incorrect Behavior: The plotId in the toilerState mapping remains 1 
											 instead of being updated to 2.
```
toilerState[1234] = ToilerState({
    lastToilDate: 1825564624,  // new timestamp
    plotId: 1,                 // Incorrectly remains 1 instead of 2
    landlord: 0x123...,        // Address of the landlord remains the same
    latestTaxRate: 600,        // Latest tax rate 
    dirty: false               // Dirty flag remains false
});
```

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
```
// Update the plotId in the toilerState mapping
 toilerState[tokenId].plotId = plotId;

```


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L195


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

There are certain smart contracts that do not support ERC721, using transferFrom() may result in the NFT being sent to such contracts.

In `LandManager::unstakeMunchable()` is executed:

```Javascript
munchNFT.transferFrom(address(this), mainAccount, tokenId);
```

However, if mainAccount is a contract address that does not support ERC721, the NFT can be frozen in that contract.

As per the documentation of EIP-721:

```
A wallet/broker/auction application MUST implement the wallet interface if it will accept safe transfers.
```

Ref: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-721

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider using safeTransferFrom() instead of transferFrom().



## Assessed type

ERC721

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232-L310
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L162-L168


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The user won't be able to farm their plots or `unstake` due to the txn always panic reverting. Leading to loss of funds and DOS

## Proof of Concept

The problem arises whenever `PRICE_PER_PLOT` gets increased through `configUpdated`

The problem is that whenever it gets increased, then `_getNumPlots` will return less Numbers for that `LandLord`
cause its denominated by `PRICE_PER_PLOT`

```solidity
File: LandManager.sol
344:     function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
345:         return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
346:     }
```

For example:
- a user is staked in plotId 100, and the LandLord has 200 Plots
- `PRICE_PER_PLOT` gets increased and makes the Plots of that Landlord to be 90

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258

## Impact
Bigger rewards for invalid `plotId`

The wrong logical operator will make that invalid `plotId` to have full rewards instead of limited rewards calculated with `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` as `timestamp`

## Proof of Concept

Before the overview of the bug we first need to know that `PlotId` = 0 is a valid Plot.

This also evidenced in `stakeMunchable` as we see here

```solidity
File: LandManager.sol
146:         if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```
We make sure that `plotId != totalPlotsAvail` so that a LandLord with 0 Plots can't have users staking on PlotId = 0 

This shows that always the valid `PlotId` can't be equal to the number of plots. In simpler terms, its desgined so that valid PlotId are the ones < NumPlots of that LandLord.

With that in mind,

Whenever a LandLord unlock some funds -> his `NumPlots` will dcrease due to this equation 

```solidity
File: LandManager.sol
344:     function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
345:         return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
346:     }
```

For a users who staked on that landLord before he unlocked some funds, there can be users having PlotIds >= `NumPlots` of that LandLord due to the funds unlocked.

Now when those users call functions that call `_farmPlots` we do the following check
```solidity
File: LandManager.sol
258:             if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
259:                 timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
260:                 toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
261:             }
```

The problem in that `if` is that it checks for `_toiler.plotId` that is > but it didn't take into consideration the `plotId` that is = to `NumPlots` cause these Plot should be now invalid as provided by the information above

Now plotId that is = to `NumPlots` will get full rewards cause its timeStamp will be assigned to `block.timestamp` in the `for` Loop, although it should have gotten its reward calculated from `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated`, but due to the wrong operator (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId instead of <=) that specific `plotId` will have full rewards.


## Tools Used
Manaul review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Put the right logical operator instead of the wrong one 
```diff
-           if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
+           if (_getNumPlots(landlord) <= _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

Invalid Validation

```solidity
232:     function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
.////////////////////OmitCode
270:             finalBonus =
271:                 int16(
272:                     REALM_BONUSES[

284:                 (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
285:                     (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
286:             );
.////////////////////OmitCode
```

we see in Line 270 the `finalBonus` is by adding `REALM_BONUSES` to `RARITY_BONUSES`

- RARITY_BONUSES = [0, 0, 10, 20, 30, 50]
- REALM_BONUSES =[ 10, -10, -5, 0, 5, -10, 10, -5, 5, 0, -5, 0, 10, 5, -10, 0, -5, 10, 10, -10, 5, 10, 0, -10, 10,]

the problem is that the `finalBonus` can be negative when combining those indexes here
- - REALM_BONUSES is = [1,2,5,7,10,14,16,19,23] 
- - index of RARITY_BONUSES is = [0,1]

Now taking into considerations that `finalBonus` can be negative then the problem arises in the following equation 

```solidity
File: LandManager.sol
283:             schnibblesTotal = uint256(
284:                 (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
285:                     (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
286:             );
```

Here we calculate (Schnibbles + (schnibbles * negative value)) / 100

Lets take an Example to show why the above equation is wrong:

- lets Assume that `schnibblesTotal` = 400, `finalBonus` = - 10 then the equation will be the following 
- - (400 + (400 * - 10)) / 100 - >
- - (400 + (-4000)) / 100 ->
- - (-3600) / 100 = -36

Now we we cast -36 to uint256 At Line 283 this will cause underflow and will have a value of `type(uint256).max - 36`

manual testing

```diff

-                   (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
```

```
    toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
```

2. The `schnibblesTotal` calculation will be wrong for this token, not only for the current farming round, but also for all future rounds. Because it should've been marked as `true` for `dirty`, but it didn't.

In a nutshell, the design of the game is broken by the code, and the scale of the impact is large. Both the parties of `renters` and `landlords` are impacted on their yield calculation. Therefore, this bug is a `High` severity issue to the game.

Firstly, there are other 2 places of code where it is using the correct logic. Change that piece of code to `if (_getNumPlots(landlord) <= _toiler.plotId)`.

This causes a logical discrepancy where the toiler is visually in the new plot but their state still reflects the old plotId, leading to potential inconsistencies and issues with further interactions that depend on the correct `plotId`. This bug has a wide scale of impact on MANY things, to name a few:
1. Erroneous interactions by other functions that rely on accurate `plotId`. For example, the `toilerState[tokenId].dirty` can be totally messed up, because in the `_farmPlots` function there is a piece of logic to update this state variable relying on the `toilerState[tokenId].plotId`;
2. This discrepancy can also be exploited by sophisticated users to find loopholes in tax calculations exploiting the mismatch in staking visibility vs actual location in the contract's logic;
3. ...etc.

Therefore, it is absolutely a `High` severity bug.

## Proof of Concept
1. **Initial Setup:**
   - Assume a user `Alice` has a toiler with `tokenId=123` staked in `plotId=5` on a land owned by `landlordBob`. The `toilerState` for `tokenId=123` shows `plotId=5`.
   
2. **Triggering the Transfer:**
   - Alice decides to move her toiler `tokenId=123` from `plotId=5` to an unoccupied `plotId=10` within the same landlord space or another.
   - She executes `transferToUnoccupiedPlot(tokenId=123, plotId=10)`.

3. **Behind the Scenes:**
   - The function verifies that `plotId=10` is not occupied (`plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][plotId].occupied == false`).
   - It proceeds to execute the transfer: it sets the old `plotOccupied[landlordBob][5]` to unoccupied and the new `plotOccupied[landlordBob][10]` to occupied by `tokenId=123`.
   - It updates `toilerState[tokenId=123].latestTaxRate` to the current tax rate for the new plot.
   - **However, it fails to update `toilerState[tokenId=123].plotId` to `10`, leaving it as `5`.**

4. **Post-Transfer State:**
   - Anyone querying the state of `tokenId=123` will see it incorrectly still staked at `plotId=5`, even though interactions and tax computations apply as if it is on `plotId=10`.
   - This can lead to misleading information displayed to the user, potentially incorrect tax calculations, or even erroneous interactions by other functions that rely on accurate `plotId`.


## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Just add a line to update the `plotId`:
```solidity
    ...
    toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]
        .currentTaxRate;
    toilerState[tokenId].plotId = plotId; // Add this line to update the plotId correctly
    plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][oldPlotId] = Plot({
        occupied: false,
        tokenId: 0
    });
    ...
```


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L140


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The logic in the `stakeMunchable` function checks if the length of `munchablesStaked[mainAccount]` is strictly greater than 10 and reverts the transaction if true (`TooManyStakedMunchiesError`). However, this does not prevent exactly 11 munchables from being staked due to the inequality used (`> 10` ). This allows an account to stake one additional munchable than the intended maximum limit.

This bug presents an oversight and results in the code deviating from its supposed functional limitation. The intended invariant of not allowing staking more than 10 munchables is broken due to this misalignment in the conditional statement logic.

## Proof of Concept
1. **Prerequisites:**
   - An account (let’s call it `Alice`) must be registered and linked with a main account.
   - `Alice` must own at least 11 munchable NFTs that are approved for the contract.
   - Ensure that a landlord address (not equal to Alice's main account) has sufficient plots available for staking.

2. **Execution:**
   - `Alice` calls `stakeMunchable` with the landlord’s address and the token IDs of her munchables up to 10 munchables successfully. The checks for registration, plot availability, ownership, and approval will pass, and these munchables will be correctly transferred and tracked within the contract.
   - Execute the `stakeMunchable` function an eleventh time with another valid munchable token ID owned by `Alice`. Since the check looks for `munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length > 10` and at this point the length is exactly 10, the check does not trigger the revert. Thus, the eleventh munchable is also successfully staked.

3. **Outcome:**
   - `Alice` ends up with 11 munchables staked, one more than intended by the contract limit.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Adjust the conditional check within the `stakeMunchable` function to include equality:
```
if (munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length >= 10)
    revert TooManyStakedMunchiesError();
```


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

raw_row.title: The `triggerPlotMetadata` function is prone to back-running attack, which can force the landlord to use an undesired tax rate

title: The `triggerPlotMetadata` function is prone to back-running attack, which can force the landlord to use an undesired tax rate
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L104-L114


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `triggerPlotMetadata` function only does two things: 
1. update the timestamp
2. set the `currentTaxRate` as the `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE`

In some certain market conditions, i.e. when the market becomes competitive and the average tax rate set by the cohort of landlords is generally way higher than the `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE`, this function will become prone to back-running attack. The renters can use bots to back-run it with `stakeMunchable` function and seize these plots immediately, because that tax rate is a steal in the current market condition. Even though the landlords can use `updateTaxRate` function to update the number later, but the previous undesired `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE` number had already been written into `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`. This numbers will be the effective tax rate until the next time the renter calls the `farmPlots` function.

When they call the `farmPlots` function, the yield will be calculated using that undesired `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE` first, and then the `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` will get updated to the landlord's updated tax rate. The landlord suffers from the unfair tax rate for the whole time being, until the `farmPlots` function gets called by the renter. This leads to a loss of yield to the landlord.

## Proof of Concept
1. When `landlordBob` calls `triggerPlotMetadata()`, this [Line#110](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L110C29-L110C45) ensures `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE` is applied to him.
2. When `renterAlice`'s bot found Bob's trxn, she immediately back run it with `stakeMunchable` to seize the plot, and this [Line#166](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L166) makes the undesired `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE` get written into `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`.
3. When Alice calls `farmPlots` function, this [Line#288](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L288) leads to the undesired `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE` is used for the whole time being; only after the calculation is finished, this [Line#292-293](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L292-L293) updates the landlord's new tax rate to be effective.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Revise the `triggerPlotMetadata` function to make it take an additional param -- the intended tax rate, to be passed in by the caller, and use that instead of using the `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE`.


## Assessed type

Other

raw_row.title: Landlords can deliberately cheat in the game to earn yield via tax without effectively keeping their fund locked in the game

title: Landlords can deliberately cheat in the game to earn yield via tax without effectively keeping their fund locked in the game
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The code has a logic hole which can be exploited by the cohort of landlord that they only need to lock their fund at two key timepoints and then unlock it immediately after the `minDuration` has passed --- they do not have to keeping it locked but still can achieve the same effect on the yield as if their fund has been locked for the whole time being.

These two key timepoints are:
1. At the beginning timepoint when the renters stake their Munchables
2. At the timepoint of the renters having the action of farming the plots. The landlords can use bots to listen to their renter's pending trxns of `farmPlots` or `unstakeMunchable`, and front-run it with staking funds again.

In the POC section I'll explain why this cheating behavior can achieve the same effect as if the landlord's fund had been kept locked for the whole time being. 

Because this cheating scenario works generally, so every landlord can adopt it to unfairly get more yield then they should have been entitled to, making this impact one in the large scale. Hence it is an Medium severity.

## Proof of Concept
1. Assume that initially the landlord staked their fund normally, and at `t0` a renter came to stake a Munchable at the landlord's plotId of 0;
2. After the Munchable was staked, the landlord decided that instead keeping his fund locked, he'd unlock it immediately when it's allowed to(`minDuration` passed).  Assume that he unlocked it at `t1`;
3. Later at `t2`, the renter began to submit farming actions. The landlord's bot was listening to this and immediately front-run it with staking funds again. So, at `t2` when the farming action was executed, the `_getNumPlots(landlord)` went up again, leading to these results:
    * The renter's Munchable will NOT be marked as `dirty`;
    * The renter gets full yield for the whole time being as if the landlord's plot had always been active, therefore, the landlord will get his full tax yield as well. 
4. However, we can see that for the period between `t1` and `t2` the landlord actually had no locked fund, hence shouldn't have any yield for this period. They effectively cheated to get more yield than they should've been entitled to.
5. This cheating scenario can be easily amplified in the perspectives below:
    * ALL landlords can use this strategy, and everybody can cheat to get the `t1~t2` yield. In reality, depending on the cases of the renters' activity frequency, the `t1~t2` can potentially mean a significant amount of time.
    * My illustration above is using one plot as a simplified example, but in reality this can be amplified to multiple or all plots that a certain landlord may own, depending on the scale of fund they decided to cheat upon.

For the reasons above, the impact can be amplified to a quite large scale, which makes it no longer "_an edge case_" but rather a general case. The whole game's integrity in the design is ruined by this cheating strategy.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Move the relevant logic of labeling `dirty` and force to farm the yield of the impacted staked `tokenId`s into the logic of the landlord's `unstake` function, so that the related pieces get updated in real time and keep the game fair.





## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L18
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L277-L279


# Vulnerability details

## Description

RARITY_BONUSES is defined as uint8[] as follows:

```solidity
uint8[] RARITY_BONUSES;
```
uint8 has 8 bits and it handle at most 2^8 - 1. uint8 to int8 conversion is unsafe due to missing bit. int8 store sign bit and it can handle at most 2^7 - 1.
So, basicly every value between 128 to 255 will be panicked. Also, after this conversion it directly convert int8 to int16 which isn't necessary. Directly converting uint8 to int16 is a safe operation.

## Impact
Functionality problem
Can't set higher value than 127 to RARITY_BONUSES if it's setted by storage players who have massive rarity bonus can't farm the plots.

## Proof of Concept
In order to illustrate this behaviour, following function can be runned to see the result:

```solidity
function test_UnsafeCasting() public {
  uint8 a = 128;
  int8 b = int8(a);
}
```

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Removing int8() casting will solve the problem


## Assessed type

Math

# Vulnerability details

## Description
plotId is defined as uint256 and it can start from 0 index to n index. If a landlord have 3 max plot, basicly 0,1,2 indexes are available for plot. We can also see this behaviour from following lines:

```solidity
uint256 totalPlotsAvail = _getNumPlots(landlord);
if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```

It uses ```>=``` instead of ```>``` because index 0 is counted as available plot.
In edge case, players total farm time calculated using lastUpdated time, but normally it's calculated with block.timestamp which generate more reward than edge case. 
But in following lines, while deciding the plotId is whether in edge case or not. It uses ```<``` operator and it should be ```<=``` for correct calculation:

```solidity
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```
 
## Impact
- Main functionality problem
- While calculation of edge case, ```plotId == maxPlot``` case calculated wrongly and player can farm more reward.  

## Proof of Concept
In order to illustrate this, we can use following scenario:

- Alice is landlord and she have 4 plots ( _getNumPlots(landlord) )
- Those plot ids are 0, 1, 2, 3
- Bob has a plot whose id's 3
- Then Alice make some changes and now she have 3 plots
- Normally, bob's plot should be dirty right now because remainning plot ids are 0, 1, 2
- Now, bob can farm his plot without being catched in if statement and it can farm his plot using block.timestamp variable.
- So, it will generate more reward to him

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Changing ```<``` operator to ```<=``` will solve the problem

Other

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can occupy the plot for a long time but do not allow the landowner to receive Schnibbles.

## Proof of Concept
background:
1. The user will occupy the landowner's plot, and then receive Schnibbles through the `_farmPlots` function. The Schnibbles will be distributed to the user and the landowner in proportion.
2. In the `_farmPlots` function, [whether a piece of land is dirty is determined based on the landlord's pledge. There are two situations where users can prevent landowners from receiving Schnibbles.
1. The user never receives Schnibbles but always occupies this plot.
2. After the landlord withdraws the funds, the polt becomes dirty, and the landlord stakes again. The land will not become non-dirty. Schnibbles no longer spawn. Users can occupy the plot without taking out the NFT.

User failure to claim may be malicious or unintentional.
Since there is a risk of funds being locked, it satisfies High, but the possibility is low because users do not get rewards. So I think the risk is Med.

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended that landowners also call the `farmPlots` function to receive Schnibbles.

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Since the `farmPlots` function will update the landlord's `lastPetMunchable`, the user can continuously call the `farmPlots` function to prevent the landlord from petting.

## Proof of Concept
background:

Landowners need to use the [`pet` function](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/SnuggeryManager.sol#L208-L233) to receive different Schnibbles. The `pet` function has a calling time limit and can only be called 10 minutes after `lastPetMunchable` has been updated.
```solidity
    function pet(address _pettedOwner, uint256 _tokenId) external notPaused {
    ···
        if (pettedAttributes.lastPettedTime + 5 minutes > block.timestamp)
            revert PettedTooSoonError();
        if (_petterPlayer.lastPetMunchable + 10 minutes > block.timestamp)
            revert PetTooSoonError();
```

So users can continuously call the `farmPlots` function to continuously update the landlord's `lastPetMunchable`. As a result, the landlord cannot call the pet function.

This gives attackers the possibility to prevent landowners from receiving Schnibbles. Caused financial losses. However, the attack cost is high and it needs to be called every 10 minutes, so I judged it to be MEd.

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended to update mainAccount's lastPetMunchable in the `_farmPlots` function instead of updating landlord's lastPetMunchable.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L173-L197


# Vulnerability details

In LandManager.sol, two of the functions are stakeMunchable() and unstakeMunchable(). Both have the `notPaused` modifier. This means that the functions are not executed during a suspended state. However, there is no functionality to retrieve staked MUNCH tokens for users if the contract is paused.

## Impact
Users may permanently lose their MUNCH tokens as they will be not able to unstake due to paused state of the contract.

## Proof of Concept

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175

1. Bob stake MUNCH tokens.
2. By any reason the contract gets temporary/permanently paused.
3. Bob MUNCH tokens are lost for the duration of the pause. It may be forever.

In this case all staked MUNCH tokens are going to be blocked temporary/permanently.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider a backup plan for this situation with which MUNCH token owners will be always able to unstake their tokens.


## Assessed type

Token-Transfer

title: `toilerState[tokenId].poolId` is not changed when `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` is called
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L199-L226


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
when calling `function transferToUnoccupiedPlot(uint256 tokenId, uint256 plotId)` the `toilerState[tokenId].plotId` is not set to the new `plotId`.
This means that when unstaking with `function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId)`, the new plot to which the stake was transferred is not erased.
The impact is that when a stake is transferred to an occupied plot, it is set permanently and cannot be erased even if the user un-stakes.

## Proof of Concept

consider the following, there are two unoccupiedPlots, `uint256 plotId1` and `uint256 plotId2`,
user Bob wants to stake the token `uint256 tokenId` to `address landlord` at `plotId1`.

after staking
```solidity
plotOccupied[landlord][plotId1] = Plot({
            occupied: true,
            tokenId: tokenId
        });
```

while 
```solidity
plotOccupied[landlord][plotId2] = Plot({
            occupied: false,
            tokenId: 0
        });
```

user bob then calls `function transferToUnoccupiedPlot(uint256 tokenId, uint256 plotId)`, with `plotId2` as the second argument
at the end of the call

```solidity
plotOccupied[landlord][plotId1]` = Plot({
            occupied: false,
            tokenId: 0
        });
```

while 
```solidity
plotOccupied[landlord][plotId2]` = Plot({
            occupied: true,
            tokenId: tokenId
        });
```

when user Bob then un-stakes the token, since the `plotOccupied` was not updated when `function transferToUnoccupiedPlot` was called, the storage remains the same, and `plotOccupied[landlord][plotId2]` is permanently occupied.

## Tools Used
Manual Audit

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
in `transferToUnoccupiedPlot(uint256 tokenId, uint256 plotId)`  set the `poolId` in the `toilerState` with

```solidity
toilerState[tokenId].plotId = poolId;
```





## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L213-L222


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Owners of NFTs (Munchables) can stake their tokens inside the `LandManager` contract and receive rewards in the process. Through the `transferToUnoccupiedPlot()`, they can change the `plotId` for their token. The function however does not correctly update the struct stored in the storage inside the `toilerState` mapping. Inside the function, the only variable updated from the `ToilerState` struct is `latestTaxRate`. The `plotId` is not updated, which could lead to a loss of rewards/schnibbles for the owner of the NFT/s.

## Proof of Concept
Let's say a landlord by the name of Alice has 10 plots available based on their `LockedWeightedValue`. The owner of a NFT with id of 3 (Bob) decided to stake his token to plot №10 (plotId = 9).

1. Bob calls `stakeMunchable(0xAl1ce, 3, 9)`.

2. After one week, Alice withdraws some of her locked funds and based on the calculation inside `_getNumPlots()`, she now has only 5 available plots -> a reduction from 10 to 5. Let's also assume that Bob called `farmPlots()` and got his rewards for the 1 week during he had staked.

3. Bob decides to change the plot for his NFT from 9 to 4, because plot №5 is still NOT occupied and has the lowest taxes of the newly available plots. In the process of calling `transferToUnoccupiedPlot()`, he will claim schnibbles before the fn executes (Due to the `forceFarmPlots` modifier). However only `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` storage variable will be updated and NOT `toilerState[tokenId].plotId`. The change (The update of `plotId`) will be reflected only for the `plotOccupied` mapping on the following lines.

4. After one more week, Bob calls `farmPlots()`, he will claim once again the according rewards for staking for one week, however because `toilerState` mapping has NOT been updated properly, the `plotId` will still be 9 and the condition on line 258 (https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258) will pass, marking the `ToilerState` as "dirty".

5. After 2 more weeks, Bob decides to withdraw his `Munchable`. The `forceFarmPlots` will be executed prior to the function body, but since the `toiler` is dirty, the condition on line 251 (https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251) will pass and no rewards will be given/awarded for the last 2 weeks.

As a conclusion, Bob received only rewards for the 2 out of the total 4 weeks during which he had staked his token, leading to loss of rewards.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Update the `plotId` storage variable -> `toilerState[tokenId].plotId = plotId;`


## Assessed type

Other
