# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L181-L184


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When a user stakes on a `plot Id` and they decide to transfer to another `unoccupied plot Id`, when the user `unstakes` from the plot Id they moved to they render that plot Id associated with the landlords main account  `useless(meaning no other user can stake to that plotId) forever`, regardless of if the landlord `locks or unlocks`.

E.g user stakes their token Id on `plot Id 4` and transfers to `plot Id 6`. Once the user `unstakes` from `plotId 6`. No other user can stake on that landlords `plot Id 6` ever.

Landlord `locks tokens` in order to have a certain number of plots that they can use to `earn schnibbles` from users staking in them. Users transfering their token Id from their current plot Id to unoccupied plot Id's are `natural phenomena` that should happen in the LandManager contract `without consequence`. If this happens over and over again due to the natural activity of transferring from plot to plot, almost all the lands owned by the landlords main account can be rendered useless.

## Proof of Concept
This occurs due to the improper updating of the toiler state plotId in the `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` function.

We'll take a scenario of a userA staking their `token Id 3` on `landlord: Alice` `plot 5` and then transferring to `plot 6`.
Then userB or any user not being able to stake on `plot 6`

We'll keep track of the following things we need after every action:
toilerState[tokenId].plotId
plotOccupied[landlord][plotId].occupied

- userA stakes `tokenId 3` on landord Alice `plot Id 5` by calling `stakeMunchable`

 toilerState[3].plotId = 5
 plotOccupied[Alice][5].occupied = true

- userA transfers`tokenId 3` on landord Alice from `plot Id 5` to unoccupied `plot Id 6` by calling `transferToUnoccupiedPlot`

 toilerState[3].plotId = 5
 plotOccupied[Alice][5].occupied = false
 plotOccupied[Alice][6].occupied = true

The toiler state plot Id isn't updated on the transferToUnoccupiedPlot to the new plot its being transferred to

- userA unstakes `tokenId 3` on landord Alice from `plot Id 6` by calling `unstakeMunchable`

  This is the code that updates the occupied status for the plot Id 
 `plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][_toiler.plotId] = Plot({occupied: false, tokenId: 0});`

  Since the `toiler.landlord = alice` & `the toiler.plotId = 5`
  **This is because on transferring the plot the toiler plot Id wasn't updated**
  This is what happens even though
  plotOccupied[Alice][5].occupied = false
  plotOccupied[Alice][6].occupied = true // this isn't updated at all
  toilerState[3].plotId = 0

- userB tries to stake `tokenId 21` on landord Alice `plot Id 6` by calling `stakeMunchable`
  
  plotOccupied[Alice][6].occupied = true

  userB or any other user `always reverts` because even though `userA has unstaked` from `plot Id 6`
  The plot Id 6 will always show as `occupied = true`

  A check is always made before a munchable is staked to a plot Id which is
  `if (plotOccupied[landlord][plotId].occupied) {
      revert OccupiedPlotError(landlord, plotId);
   }`
  Meaning this check would always revert for affected plots.
  
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Updating the toiler state plot Id in the `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` function.





## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L280-L282


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Whenever admin roles update the price of the a configured token in the LockManager Contract Through a proposal successfully. If its a decrease in price it can render some existing plot Id's dirty when calculating rewards for present and future in the `_farmPlots()` function even without the landlord locking or unlocking their tokens.

In some cases a users NFT can be stuck in the contract until the Landlord locks, unlocks tokens or increases lock duration forcing a plot metadata update.

## Proof of Concept

Lets look at the following actions:
- A landlord has `10 plots` of lands existing and decides to increase his lock duration in the LockManager contract. This in turn calls the `accountManager.forceHarvest()` which updates the plot metadata. Lets take the time this happened at `second x + 100`. Where x is a starting time at some point for all future times.

- A user stakes onto the landlords `plot Id 9` in the LandManger contract. Then at `second x + 160` decides to manually farm his plots via `farmPlots()` or `transferToUnoccupiedPlot()` if he's moving to another plot Id.

- At `second x + 200` there is a proposal in the lockManager that was accepted to decrease the usd price of a configured token the landlord has locked. This in turn reduces the number of plots that the landlord has via the `_getNumPlots` function.

- If the number of plots the landlord has reduces to 7. It means the users plot Id is now dirty without the landlord locking or unlocking any tokens.

- When the user decides to call `unstakeMunchable` the `_farmPlots()` function is called and this function reverts because of an arithmetic underflow in the `_farmplots()`:

`if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
    timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
    toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
`}
Since the users plot Id is now less, due to the proposal to decrease the price of a configured token in the LockManager has passed.
The toiler plot Id : `9` is now dirty and the timestamp for calculating rewards for the toiler is now the last updated timestamp of the landlord plotMetadata.
Which was the last time the landlord, locked, unlocked or increased lock duration and that was at `second x + 100`

Further down in the `_farmPlots()` function,

`schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;`

The schnibblesTotal is a uint256 value.
The timestamp is the last updated plot metadata of the landlord which is `second x + 100`
The toiler last toil date was the last time the toiler directly or indirectly called `_farmPlots()` which was at `second x + 160`.

`schnibblesTotal = ((x+100) - (x+160)) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;`


This means the schnibblesTotal would revert every time due to the arithmetic underflow in the logic when the user tries to `transferToUnoccupiedPlot()`, `unstakeMunchable()` or `farmPlot()` until the landlord associated with the toiler(tokenId) either locks more tokens, unlocks tokens or increases his lock duration. 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Another function for a user to unstake their token Id without farming plots in the process.








## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L281


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The tx to call `_farmPlots()` will be reverted due to the incorrect usage of `timestamp`, leading to DoS of contract and users lose their NFT.

## Proof of Concept

The usages of variable `timestamp`:

l. L248: Initiated to `block.timestamp`
2. L259: Set to `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` if `_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId`

However, this reassignment can lead to an issue where `timestamp` becomes smaller than `_toiler.lastToilDate`, causing the calculation at line 281 to revert.

```solidity
232:     function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
...
247:         for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
248:             timestamp = block.timestamp;
...
258:             if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
259:                 timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
260:                 toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
261:             }
...
280:             schnibblesTotal =
281:                 (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * // <= reverts
282:                 BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

Consider the following scenario:

1.  The `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` is set to 2024-07-01.
2.  An NFT, having been farmed earlier, has its `toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate` set to 2024-08-01.
3.  The NFT's `plotId` becomes unfit due a reduction in locked weight.
4.  The condition `_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId` is true, leading to `timestamp` being set to `plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` (2024-07-01).
5.  The subtraction `timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate` becomes negative (2024-07-01 - 2024-08-01), causing the transaction to revert.

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Ensure that `timestamp` is always greater than or equal to `_toiler.lastToilDate`. A check should be added to verify this condition before performing the subtraction.










## Assessed type

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The variable `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` does not track the latest tax rate, resulting in inaccurate `schnibblesLandlord` calculation.

## Proof of Concept

In `_farmPlots()`, the `schnibblesLandlord` is calculated utilizes `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`. However, the actual latest tax rate is stored in `plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord].currentTaxRate`, which is updated AFTER the latest tax rate is used to calculate the `schnibblesLandlord`:

```solidity
287:             schnibblesLandlord =
288:                 (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate) / <= used before updating
289:                 1e18;
290: 
291:             toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate = timestamp;
292:             toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord] // <= updated after the schnibblesLandlord calc
293:                 .currentTaxRate;
```

The reason `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` is outdated:

- The `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` is updated when [`stakeMunchable()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L166), [`transferToUnoccupiedPlot()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L213) and [`_farmPlots()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L292).

- If users call `updateTaxRate()` to change `plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate` after the aforementioned changes for `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate`, the `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` is no longer the latest tax rate.

## Tools Used
manual

Update `toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate` to the latest tax rate before using:

```diff
+            toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]

-            toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]
-                .currentTaxRate;
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

There are two cases for this issue:

1. Inadequate handling of the exit mechanism in the `_farmPlots` function may result in scenarios where valid plots remain invalid, preventing users from earning rewards. Additionally, the landlord's plot utilization rate may be reduced by 20% or more due to the impact of currency price fluctuations.
2. The second case, while theoretically possible, is less likely to occur but can still affect users. In this situation, the landlord cannot receive rewards if the staked user does not perform any operations, and the landlord cannot do anything to trigger the rewards. Although this situation exists in theory, users will be motivated to collect rewards to end this state. However, the landlord's time will be affected as it depends on the actions of the staked user.

## Proof of Concept

For the second case, the issue is clear.

The main focus here is the first case, the key point [code snippet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251) in the `_farmPlots` function:

```solidity
            if (_toiler.dirty) continue;
```

```solidity
            landlord = _toiler.landlord;
            // use last updated plot metadata time if the plot id doesn't fit
            // track a dirty bool to signify this was done once
            // the edge case where this doesnt work is if the user hasnt farmed in a while and the landlord
            // updates their plots multiple times. then the last updated time will be the last time they updated their plot details
            // instead of the first
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

Consider the following scenario:

1. A plot becomes invalid due to reduced locked funds or token price drop, and the dirty flag will be set after the user's daily farm (user behavior is uncertain, but what is clear is that users may have a need for daily harvesting that).
2. If funds are relocked or the price rises, the plot remains invalid since the dirty flag isn't reset.
3. Users must restake to earn rewards; otherwise, they receive nothing even if the plot is valid again.

For the landlord, he has to wait for other users to perform operations. Even if he wants to lock more funds to remedy the invalid plot caused by the price drop, it will be of no avail. If the staked user wants to act maliciously or doesn't notice this, it could result in a denial of service for the landlord.

Unlike the effect of calling lock/unlock directly, price changes are beyond the control of users.

As an example, ETH's price fluctuations in the last month have ranged from around [2800-3500 (refer CMC)](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/ethereum/), the percentage change in the price of ETH over the last 30 days is approximately 20%.
 ​
This means that for a landlord who locks in ETH, 20% of his plots may remain “invalid” due to price fluctuations, while the ETH price will keep changing, which will reduce the landlord's utilization of his plots by 20%.

## Tools Used

Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1. If the plot is no longer available (unlocking funds/price change), remove the munchable occupying the plot directly during function processing (unlock) or give the landlord the option of triggering an unstake operation (Since no revenue is generated when plots are invalidated after farming and dirty flag are set up, there is no loss for staked munchable users and there is an opportunity to shift the gas cost).

2. Landlords should have the option to set a maximum farming time for plots. This should be a two-way choice. Once farming is complete, both the landlord and the user can opt out (or harvest) and move on to the next round of farming. This mitigation is also an alternative solution to the known critical problem described in the README (the edge case where plots are updated multiple times) by adding a variable that keeps a record of the actual farming time, and the validity time of the plots affected by the lock/unlock operations is stored. (More details will be discussed in that issue)
















## Assessed type

Context

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L138


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
After transferring the `tokenId` to a new unoccupied plot, the `plotId` in the `toiletState` is not updated with the new `plotId`.

Imagine we have the following scenario (for the example below, the landlord is not changed):
1. Bob stakes his `tokenId` to `plotId = 1`.
2. Bob decides to transfer his `tokenId` to a new unoccupied plot after 3 days, for example, `plotId = 3`.
3. After 10 days, Bob unstakes his `tokenId`.
4. After a few days, he stakes his `tokenId` again to the same plotId = 3, but his transaction will fail because `plotOccupied[landlord][plotId].occupied == ture`.


This happens because after unstaking a munchable token, the `plotOccupied` is reset, as the `_toiler.plotId` is equal to the old `tokenId`.

```solidity
//@audit _toiler.plotId = oldPlotId
plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][_toiler.plotId] = Plot({
            occupied: false,
            tokenId: 0
        });
```

During the transfer, the `toiletState` is not updated with the new `plotId`, as only the `plotOccupied` is changed.

```solidity
plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][oldPlotId] = Plot({
            occupied: false,
            tokenId: 0
        });

        plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][plotId] = Plot({
            occupied: true,
            tokenId: tokenId
        });
```

This breaks the following sequence of actions: `transferring` -> `unstaking` -> `staking` to the same plotId where the token was transferred. 

This limits users because if they transfer a token and unstake, they cannot stake their token to the same plot again, which may lead to earning fewer schnibbles.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L215-L223

For the toilerState struct, after transferring the token to a new unoccupied plot, change the `plotId` to the new `plotId`.

In `_farmPlots` internal function there is a code that check to set `toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true` when landload's plots number is less than `toilerState[tokenId].plotId` which will pass even when the landload has 0 plot and `toilerState[tokenId].plotId = 0` because 0 is not less than 0.
```javascript
if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
    timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
    toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
}
```

Even though in publicly known issues it was mentioned that the above check has something to look at but that referred to getting timestamp for calculating schnibblesTotal not about users that staked at plotId 0.

## Proof of Concept
The following scenario shows how Bob can take advantage of staking at plotId 0 to farm even when landload has no plots.

1. Bob staked his MunchableNFT to plotId 0 of Alice(landload).
2. Bob call `farmPlots()` after a day to farm his plot for schnibbles.
3. Alice reduce his locked asset to an amount that can not buy a single plot. Now Alice have 0 plot.
4. Bob can continue to call `farmPlots()` successfully even though the landload has no plotId.  

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change the check condition to be less than or equals to since user can not stake at plotId that is equals to landload's plot number in `stakeMunchable` function.
```
if (_getNumPlots(landlord) <= _toiler.plotId) {
    timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
    toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
}
```

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L199
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L29
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/interfaces/ILandManager.sol#L7


# Vulnerability details

## Vulnerability Description 

Main purpose of [transferToUnoccupiedPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L199) function is to transfer Munchable (TokenId) from one Plot to another plot and it then update the [plotOcuppied](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L215-L222) mapping correctly and update the tax to [latestTaxRate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L213). But, The issues lies in the [transferToUnoccupiedPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L199) function where it neglects to update the plotId of Munchable TokenId in it's [Toiler'sState Mapping](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L29) leading to an incorrectness between the actual location of the Munchable and its recorded state.

## Code Snippet

[transferToUnoccupiedPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L199)

```solidity
function transferToUnoccupiedPlot(
        uint256 tokenId,
        uint256 plotId
    ) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
        (address mainAccount, ) = _getMainAccountRequireRegistered(msg.sender);
        ToilerState memory _toiler = toilerState[tokenId];
        uint256 oldPlotId = _toiler.plotId;
        uint256 totalPlotsAvail = _getNumPlots(_toiler.landlord);
        if (_toiler.landlord == address(0)) revert NotStakedError();
        if (munchableOwner[tokenId] != mainAccount) revert InvalidOwnerError();
        if (plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][plotId].occupied)
            revert OccupiedPlotError(_toiler.landlord, plotId);
        if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();

        toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]
            .currentTaxRate;
        plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][oldPlotId] = Plot({
            occupied: false,
            tokenId: 0
        });
        plotOccupied[_toiler.landlord][plotId] = Plot({
            occupied: true,
            tokenId: tokenId
        });
        //@audit  Missing: Update toilerState[tokenId].plotId
        emit FarmPlotLeave(_toiler.landlord, tokenId, oldPlotId);
        emit FarmPlotTaken(toilerState[tokenId], tokenId);
    }
```

## Proof of Concept

1. Initial State:
   - Alice is a landlord with 200 plots (0 to 199).
   - Bob owns Munchable NFT with tokenId 42.
   - Bob has staked his Munchable on Alice's plot 100.
   - Current state:
     * `plotOccupied[alice][100] = Plot(occupied: true, tokenId: 42)`
     * `toilerState[42] = ToilerState(lastToilDate: X, plotId: 100, landlord: alice, latestTaxRate: Y, dirty: false)`

2. Bob decides to move his Munchable to plot 150:
   - Bob calls `transferToUnoccupiedPlot(42, 150)`.
   - The function executes successfully, updating `plotOccupied`:
     * `plotOccupied[alice][100] = Plot(occupied: false, tokenId: 0)`
     * `plotOccupied[alice][150] = Plot(occupied: true, tokenId: 42)`
   - However, due to the vulnerability, `toilerState` is not fully updated:
     * `toilerState[42]` still has `plotId: 100` (should be 150)

3. Inconsistency Established:
   - Now we have a situation where:
     * The Munchable is actually on plot 150.
     * But `toilerState` says it's on plot 100.
4. Now, if Bob try to interact with the Munchable based on the toilerState, they might encounter issues because the plotId is incorrect.

## Impact
By not updating the ToilerState of TokenId while transferring tokenId from one plot to another unOccupied plot, The `_farmPlots` function may use the wrong plot ID, results in wrong or missed reward calculation. 

## Potential Issues 

Making this section as it creates multiple issues 

a) Incorrect Farming Calculations:

as,farmPlots function, which would typically use the plotId from toilerState, provided situation can occur

- When `_farmPlots` is called, it uses `toilerState[tokenId].plotId` to determine the plot.

- It might try to farm from plot 100, which is now empty, instead of 150.

- This could lead to missed farming rewards or incorrect calculations.

b) Incorrect Plot Management:

- If Alice tries to assign another Munchable to plot 100, the contract might allow it, thinking it's unoccupied but actually it had tokenId store of previous Munchable that is still stored there.

c) Worst case scenario:

- Multiple Munchables could end up with incorrect plot assignments in `toilerState`.

## Tools Used 

Manual Review 

## Recommended Mitigation 

To fix this, the `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` function should be updated to include toilerState mapping changes as below:

```solidity
toilerState[tokenId].plotId = newPlotId;
```

This simple addition would ensure that all state variables remain consistent, preventing the potential issue.





## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

This bug severely impacts the reward mechanism of the protocol:

- Users receive far fewer schnibbles than they should, potentially by orders of magnitude.
- The intended bonus system is effectively nullified, as bonuses reduce rewards instead of increasing them.
- This affects both renters (who receive fewer schnibbles) and landlords (who receive less tax).

## Proof of Concept

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283-L286

The bug is in the `_farmPlots` function:

```javascript
schnibblesTotal = uint256(
  (int256(schnibblesTotal) + int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100,
);
```

This calculation divides the entire sum by 100, effectively reducing the original `schnibblesTotal` to 1% of its intended value, plus a small bonus.

For example, if `schnibblesTotal` is 1000 and `finalBonus` is 10:

- Current, wrong calculation: `(1000 + (1000 * 10)) / 100 = 11`
- New, corrected calculation: `1000 + (1000 * 10 / 100) = 1100`

The current implementation reduces rewards by approximately 99% in this scenario.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Modify the calculation to apply the bonus correctly:

```diff
- schnibblesTotal = uint256(
-   (int256(schnibblesTotal) + int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100,
- );

+ schnibblesTotal = schnibblesTotal + uint256((int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100);
```

Math

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the `_farmPlots` function, the check for the `dirty` state is incorrect due to an `off-by-one` error. This error allows a plot that exceeds the number of qualified plots to bypass the check and not be marked as `dirty`.

## Proof of Concept

In the `_farmPlots` function, the check for the `dirty` state is performed as follows:

```solidity
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

The `_getNumPlots(landlord)` function returns the number of plots allowed for the `landlord`. However, if `_toiler.plotId == _getNumPlots(landlord)`, it actually exceeds the limit of plots but is still regarded as valid due to the use of the `<` operator. Since plotId can be `0`, the correct comparison should use the `<=` operator.

This can be verified in another check.

```solidity
if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```

As a result, this error allows a plot that exceeds the number of qualified plots to bypass the check and not be marked as `dirty`.

## Tools Used

Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Change `_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId` to `_getNumPlots(landlord) <= _toiler.plotId`

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L138-L139


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `stakeMunchable` function in the contract is vulnerable to a front-running attack, where a malicious user can repeatedly `front-run` and occupy a specific landlord-plotId, causing a `Denial of Service (DoS)` for legitimate users attempting to stake on the same plot.

## Proof of Concept
In the `stakeMunchable` function, users can stake on a specific `landlord-plotId`. However, there is a strict check to ensure that the plot is not already occupied.

```solidity
        if (plotOccupied[landlord][plotId].occupied) // @note front-run to take?
            revert OccupiedPlotError(landlord, plotId);
```

Due to this check, a malicious user can front-run the staking transaction and occupy the plot, effectively preventing the legitimate user from staking. For instance:

1. Alice intends to stake on ADDRESS-PLOT.
2. Observing Alice’s intent, Bob calls `stakeMunchable` to occupy the plot just before Alice’s transaction is processed, causing Alice’s staking attempt to fail.

## Tools Used

Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To mitigate this issue:
1. **Introduce a Minimum Staking Time**: Implement a minimum staking time to add a cost for front-running, making it less attractive for attackers.
2. **Iterate to Find an Unoccupied Plot**: Allow the staking function to automatically find and use an unoccupied plot if the specified plot is already occupied.


## Assessed type

DoS

```solidity
@=>         toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]
```

# Vulnerability details

## Description
When a landlord calls the `updateTaxRate` function, his/her plotMetadata.currentTaxRate is set to the newTaxRate:
```solidity
function updateTaxRate(uint256 newTaxRate) external override notPaused {
...
plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate = newTaxRate;
...
```

```solidity
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
...
schnibblesLandlord =
    (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate) /
    1e18;
...
}
```

Then, the function sets the stake/toiler's latestTaxRate to the newest one:
```solidity
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
...
toilerState[tokenId].latestTaxRate = plotMetadata[_toiler.landlord]
                .currentTaxRate;
...
}
```

The issue with that is a landlord may set a new tax rate, but the users may avoid it altogether by not calling any action at the contract. Then call the unstake function to accrue its schnibbles only when it really desires to stop using the contract, avoiding the new tax rates completely.

## Impact
Users are able to avoid new tax rates set by the landlord entirely.

Consider introducing timestamp-based epochs/periods to determine a the toiler's state, this way users cannot maliciously become inactive to avoid a landlord's taxation.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L260


# Vulnerability details

## Description
The LandManager contract sets a user's toiler state to dirty in case the landlord is not able to accommodate the plot id the user has been occupying.
This logic is determined by the amount of locked tokens held by the landlord. 
The issue with that is a plot can only become dirty in the context of the `_farmPlots` function. This function, however, is only accessible for one's own plot ids, meaning the message caller has to be a tokenId owner in order for its plot to get farmed.
The consequence of that is: in case a user detects his plotId is about to become dirty due to a landlord's unlocking of tokens, he/she can opt to avoid utilizing the LandManager contract until the landlord locks more tokens. Once this happens, the user can return to earn schnibbles - even the ones for the time period in which the landlord didn't have enough locked tokens to accommodate the plotId that was supposed to be dirty.
## Impact
The LandManager contract doesn't enforce plot's dirty status accurately and users are able to avoid losing rewards if they don't interact with the contract during the period in which their plots should be dirty.

The impact is further enhanced if we consider the landlord as a possible malicious actor: then he/she could coordinate multiple locks and unlocks to accrue rewards in a way that unfairly multiplies the amount of rewards earned.

A third impact is at the `_reconfigure` function: 
It updates the PRICE_PER_PLOT uint256 global state variable. Since this variable is utilized at the `_getNumPlots` function, it helps determine a toiler's dirty state. If a user doesn't call farmPlots often, then he/she is able to avoid the new configurations.
## Proof of Concept
**a.**
Alice is a landlord.
Bob stakes tokenId #111 to Alice's plot id #5.
Alice unlocks some tokens. Now Alice is only able to accomodate 3 plots.
Bob doesn't interact with the LandManager contract during this period.
Alice locks more tokens. Now Alice is able to accomodate 10 plots.
Bob farms its plot and earns for the whole period since its tokenId has been staked.

**b.**
Alice A. locks an amount that enables two plots to be open at her land.
Bob stakes tokenId #1 and #2. 
The unlock period passes. Alice A. unlocks this amount and sends to a sybil account of hers: Alice B..
Alice B. locks the same amount.
Bob stakes tokenId #3 and #4.
The unlock period passes. Alice B. unlocks this amount and sends to a sybil account of hers: Alice C..
Alice C. locks the same amount.
Bob stakes tokenId #5 and #6.
The unlock period passes. 40 weeks pass.
Alice C. transfers the amount to Alice A., who locks the tokens.
Bob now calls unstake for tokenId #1 and #2. He earns the rewards for the whole period in which the stake was going on.
The unlock period passes.
Alice A. transfers the amount to Alice B., who locks the tokens.
Bob now calls unstake for tokenId #3 and #4. He earns the rewards for the whole period in which the stake was going on.
The unlock period passes.
Alice B. transfers the amount to Alice C., who locks the tokens.
Bob now calls unstake for tokenId #5 and #6. He earns the rewards for the whole period in which the stake was going on.

Alice ended up having to lock 1/3 of the tokens she had given land plots to.
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider introducing timestamp-based epochs/periods to determine a toiler state's dirty status. This mechanism is interesting because it creates precise time cuts when certain sets of users ought to stop receiving rewards.
This could be really interesting for the demonstrated edge-case as it has the ability of introducing a more granular approach to a landlord's capacity and the distribution of rewards.


## Assessed type

Timing

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L213


# Vulnerability details

## Description
The transferToUnoccupiedPlot function allows users that already have staked token ids to a landlord's land to transfer to a different plot on it.
This function, however, lacks toilerState dirty updates, as it ensures the target plotId is available for the user to stake, but doesn't ensure the token ids' toiler state isn't dirty after the end of function:
```solidity
function transferToUnoccupiedPlot(
...
if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
...
}
```

## Impact
Users with dirty toiler states may transfer to an unoccupied plot but still won't be able to earn rewards on their farm actions.

## Proof of Concept
Consider Bob has staked a token at PlotId #5 of a random landowner.
The landowner unlocks some of his assets and now Bob's toilerState will become dirty as soon as he does an operation at the LandManager contract.
Attempting to keep his stake going, Bob calls transferToUnoccupiedPlot. However, as the forceFarmPlots modifier is ran, his toiler's state dirty variable is set to true.
Then at the transferToUnnocupiedPlot function is executed, but since it doesn't update the dirty state to false, Bob is not able to farm on a plotId that is supposed to be farmable.
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make sure the transferToUnnocupiedPlot function makes the toilerState dirty variable for the tokenId set to false, as the function already does sanity checks to ensure the plotId should be farmed.


## Assessed type

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L299
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/SnuggeryManager.sol#L232
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L345


# Vulnerability details

## Description
The `_farmPlots` function updates the landlords' unfedSchnibbles and its lastPetMunchable:
```solidity
landlordMetadata.unfedSchnibbles += schnibblesLandlord;
landlordMetadata.lastPetMunchable = uint32(timestamp);
```

The issue with that is, the lastPetMunchable variable is used in the context of the SnuggeryManager's contract pet function. It prevents petters who have pet for less than 10 minutes from petting again:
```solidity
function pet(address _pettedOwner, uint256 _tokenId) external notPaused {
...
if (_petterPlayer.lastPetMunchable + 10 minutes > block.timestamp)
            revert PetTooSoonError();
...
}
```

Since the farmPlots call updates the landlord's lastPetMunchable to the timestamp when a farm action has been processed to his/her land, the landlord will have a much harder time attempting to pet other munchables and may not be able to pet at all.
## Impact
Landlords may have their capacity to pet other munchables denied by the farming activity of users that stake on their land.

Users that lock tokens in the system with the intent of only getting bonuses on their pet calls at the SnuggeryManager contract may not be able to do so: as the creation of plots at the LandManager doesn't rely on any call by the landlord and can be done in a permissionless manner as long as the landlord has enough locked tokens - as the `_getNumPlots` function relies solely on the lockedWeightedValue of the possible landlord.
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make sure the `_farmPlots` function does not update the landlord's lastPetMunchable timestamp, as the landlord did not execute such action.


## Assessed type

Access Control

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L92 https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L131


# Vulnerability details

## Vulnerability details
A landlord can monitor toiler staking activities. Upon detecting a toiler's intention to stake, the landlord can front-run the toiler's `stakeMunchable()` transaction by quickly executing `updateTaxRate()` to set the tax rate to its maximum value. This action deceives the toiler into staking under unfavorable conditions. After the toiler's `stakeMunchable()` transaction is completed, the landlord can again execute `updateTaxRate()` to restore the tax rate to its original value, continuing to deceive subsequent toilers.  

## Impact
Financial Loss: Toilers may incur significant financial losses by staking under manipulated, unfavorable tax rates.  

## Proof of Concept
Prerequisites:  
- Assume the current tax rate is 10%  
- The maximum allowed tax rate is 50%  
- A Toiler is preparing to stake 1 NFT on a Landlord's plot  

Attack Steps:  

1. The Landlord monitors the mempool and detects the Toiler's `stakeMunchable()` transaction.  

2. The Landlord immediately sends an `updateTaxRate()` transaction to increase the tax rate to the maximum of 50%.  
   This transaction is set with a higher gas price than the Toiler's to ensure it's processed first by miners.  

3. Miners process the transactions in the following order:  
   a. The Landlord's `updateTaxRate()` transaction is executed, changing the tax rate to 50%.  
   b. The Toiler's `stakeMunchable()` transaction is executed, staking based on the 50% tax rate.  

4. The Toiler's stake is completed, but they only receive rights to 50% Schnibbles instead of the expected 90%.  

5. The Landlord immediately sends another `updateTaxRate()` transaction to restore the tax rate to 10%.  

6. Final Result:  
   - The Toiler loses rights to 40% Schnibbles
   - The Landlord gains an additional 40% Schnibbles in revenue  
   - The system's tax rate returns to normal, ready to deceive the next Toiler  

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1. Implement a time-lock mechanism for tax rate changes, ensuring that any modifications to the tax rate take effect after a set period (e.g., 24 hours).  

2. Modify the stakeMunchable() function to include an expectedTaxRate parameter. If the landlord's current taxRate is greater than this expected value, the transaction should revert. This change would look something like:  

```solidity
   function stakeMunchable(
        address landlord,
        uint256 tokenId,
        uint256 plotId，
        uint256 expectedTaxRate) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
            .....
            require(plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate <= expectedTaxRate, "Tax rate higher than expected");  
            // Existing staking logic  
   }  
```
   This modification allows toilers to specify their maximum acceptable tax rate, providing protection against unexpected rate increases.  


## Assessed type

MEV

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L281


# Vulnerability details

## Summary
Due to dynamic nature of checking the collaterals value when farming (checked on every farm), a users NFT can be stuck on the contract due to a underflow in subtraction on line 281.

Problem arises when in ```_farmPlots(address)``` function the ```plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated``` is used as the timestamp. However this timestamp can be lower than ```_toiler.lastToilDate``` when the USD value of landlord collateral drops thus making the users plot suddenly invalid.

## Impact
Users Munchable (NFT) is stuck on the contract permanently until the subtraction on line 281 stops underflowing.  

## Proof of Concept
Here we describe a scenario in which a users Munchable becomes bricked:
#1 - Landlord updates his lock on x timestamp
#2 - User stakes his NFT on landlords plot at x+1 timestamp
#3 - He farms his points at x+2 timestamp
#4 - The value of collateral drops and suddenly - user Munchable is on invalid plot
#5 - x will be used as timestamp and x+2 as ```_toiler.lastToilDate``` since thats the last time the user farmed.

User can not unstake/transfer his NFT because every time he tries to ```forceFarmPlots``` modifier will be called with a revert on line 281.

This issue persists until:
1. Landlord updated lock/unlock
2. Collateral gains in value thus making the plot valid again

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Not sure what solution to recommend since its entirely up to the protocol on how they want to handle these situations.
They can maybe use some other value as timestamp or continue the for loop.








## Assessed type

Under/Overflow

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L11


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Landlord get their "rent" or their tax payed by user when these two functions are called [farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L228) and [forceFarmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L40) . The `farmPlots` is used by renter manually, the `forceFarmPlots` is used when the user (renter) stake, unstake or transfer munchables to different plots - [stakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L135), [unstakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175), [transferToUnoccupiedPlot](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L202). These are all functions that are called by the renter (user who stake) not the landlord. 
The issue is that renter can by neglecting or malicious intents make landlord lose money and potential gains that are his right when he became landlord (when he get plot by locking funds).

## Proof of Concept
Imagine the following scenario:
Bob become landlord and lock funds to get the plot and want to rent it. Alice decides to stake munchable on the Bob's plot. Bob's plot get occupied and Alice start staking. But Alice decide never farm or unstake or transfer her munchables. Her munchies just sit on Bob's plot and making him occupied, but Bob never get his tax that he expect and also he can't move Alice munchies from his plot and free it for other person who wants to stake. This could go indefinitely theoretically which will make Bob the loser by not gaining desired rent(his TAX), not be able to get new user who want to stake and pay him and by that means his investment in plot will be unworthy.

The similar real world scenario:
Bob rents apartment to Alice, but Alice decides not to pay Bob the rent, and Bob not to be able to evict Alice from his apartment he rent and replace her with new residents. That would not work and Bob's investment would not be worth and he will lose money.

## Tools Used
Manual Review.
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make function that will check if user(renter) do not farm for a certain time period and give the landlords permission to remove them from his plot so it is not occupied so he can replace it with new staker. That can be manually by landlord or automatically done by protocol.





## Assessed type

Other

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blame/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Basic premise landlords lock certain amount of funds and because of that based on the amount they locked they they get plots that they can rent to other users that want to stake and therefore they payback tax to the landlords.

If landlords at some point withdraw their locked funds they should not be landlords anymore therefore users that stake on their plots should unstake and not pay any taxes to the past landlords.

Or if they withdraw certain amount they should have fewer plots available.

The issue arise in [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258) which is used by renters to pay their landlords amount the other thing, specificially with this lines of code :
```js
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```
If landlord withdraw his funds and decide not to lock anymore this will always be true and he would still receive taxes even if he should not because of the function design and because his address would still remain in `plotMetadata` mapping, it will just use last known information when metadata is updated in `lastUpdated`.
## Proof of Concept
Bob lock his funds and became a landlord. His plot metadata is created and stored in `plotMetadata` mapping with his landlord address. Alice decides to stake on Bob's plot. She start staking and paying taxes regulary and everything is in order.
After some time Bob withdraw his locked funds and is not landlord anymore. So this will always be true even if `_getNumPlots` return 0:
```js
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```
It will just use timestamp with `lastUpdated` time and Alice would pay to Bob even if he is not the landlord anymore and that plot don't exist (or should not).

After that the `lastToilDate` would get updated with timestamp as we can see here:
```js
            toilerState[tokenId].lastToilDate = timestamp;
```
 The specific value for this specific case would be: `timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated` so in the next attempt for Alice to pay she would not pay anything to Bob but also she would not earn any `schnibbles` for their munchables. Basically she would stake for nothing.

After that she can unstake from Bob's plot but she will be at loss one tax she payed to Bob that is not landlord anymore and she would not get her staking reward (schnibbles) next time.
## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Track when user is not landlord anymore, the renters should automatically be unstacked from his plots, they should pay what they owe him for that time and his plot metadata and his address should be removed from `plotMetadata` mapping. In that way the protocol will prevent renters to pay taxes to non existing landlords and to not receive rewards for staking their munchables.





## Assessed type

Other

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L228-L289


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The ``_farmPlots`` function in the ``LandManager`` contract contains a calculation that may lead to precision loss due to integer division. This could result in unfair distribution of schnibbles, potentially allowing informed users to gain an advantage over others. In extreme cases, this could lead to a drain of the contract's resources or significant imbalances in the game economy.

## Proof of Concept
The vulnerability exists in the _farmPlots function. 
An attacker analyzes the finalBonus calculation to find values that lead to favorable rounding.
They strategically choose munchables with specific realm and rarity combinations to maximize the rounding errors in their favor.
Over multiple transactions, the attacker accumulates more schnibbles than they should, gaining an unfair advantage.
Example:
Let's say schnibblesTotal is 1000 and finalBonus is 3.
The calculation would be: (1000 + (1000 * 3)) / 100 = 40
But the integer division loses the decimal, so it's actually: 1000 + 30 = 1030
An attacker could strategically time their actions to always fall just before these rounding points, accumulating extra schnibbles over time
Single Transaction Impact.Assuming thesevalues:
```
BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE = 1 schnibble per second
Time elapsed (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) = 1 day (86400 seconds)
finalBonus = 5 (5% bonus)
```
Normal calculation:
```
CopyschnibblesTotal = 86400 * 1 = 86400
bonusAmount = (86400 * 5) / 100 = 4320
totalSchnibbles = 86400 + 4320 = 90720
Actual calculation with integer division:
CopyschnibblesTotal = 86400
bonusAmount = (86400 * 5) / 100 = 4320
totalSchnibbles = 90720
```
In this case, there's no loss due to precision in a single transaction.
An attacker could exploit rounding by choosing specific time intervals:
```bash
Assume finalBonus = 1 (1% bonus)
For a 100-second interval:
schnibblesTotal = 100 * 1 = 100
bonusAmount = (100 * 1) / 100 = 1
totalSchnibbles = 101
```
For two 50-second intervals:
First interval:
```
schnibblesTotal = 50 * 1 = 50
bonusAmount = (50 * 1) / 100 = 0
totalSchnibbles = 50
```
Second interval:
```
schnibblesTotal = 50 * 1 = 50
bonusAmount = (50 * 1) / 100 = 0
totalSchnibbles = 50
```
Total for both intervals: 100
The attacker gains 1 extra schnibble by timing their actions to avoid rounding down.
Long-term Cumulative Effect assuming an attacker exploits this consistently over a year:
```
365 days * 24 hours * 60 minutes = 525,600 minutes
```
If the attacker calls ``_farmPlots`` every minute perfectly timed:
Normal user: 
```
525,600 * 60 * 1.01 = 31,861,440 schnibbles
```
Attacker: 
```
525,600 * 61 = 32,061,600 schnibbles
```
The attacker gains an extra 200,160 schnibbles over the year, which is about 0.63% more than a normal user.
Scenario 4: Large-scale Operation
Consider a large-scale farmer with 1000 munchables, each with different bonuses ranging from 1% to 10%.
In a single day:
Worst case (all 1% bonus): 86,400,000 schnibbles
Best case (all 10% bonus): 95,040,000 schnibbles
Actual case (mixed bonuses with rounding errors): ~90,720,000 schnibbles

The difference between the worst and best case is 8,640,000 schnibbles per day. If schnibbles have any real-world value (e.g., $0.01 per 1000 schnibbles), this could translate to $86.40 per day or $31,536 per year in potential manipulated gains.
The precision loss leads to a competitive advantage in several ways:
Over time, exploiters can accumulate more schnibbles than fair players, giving them an edge in the game economy.
Knowledgeable players can time their actions to always benefit from favorable rounding, consistently outperforming others.
The larger a player's operation, the more they can benefit from these small rounding errors, creating a "rich get richer" effect.
While the impact per transaction is small, the cumulative effect over time and across many users can be substantial.
## Tools Used
manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use a higher precision for calculations and only round at the final step:
```solidity
uint256 constant PRECISION = 1e18;
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
    // ... (earlier code)

    for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
        // ... (other calculations)

        int256 finalBonusScaled = int256(finalBonus) * PRECISION / 100;
        uint256 schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
        schnibblesTotal = uint256(
            (int256(schnibblesTotal) * (PRECISION + finalBonusScaled)) / PRECISION
        );

        // ... (remaining code)
    }
}
```
Consider using a library like PRBMath for fixed-point arithmetic:
```solidity
import "@prb/math/contracts/PRBMath.sol";
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
    // ... (earlier code)

    for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
        // ... (other calculations)

        int256 finalBonusScaled = PRBMath.mulDiv(int256(finalBonus), 1e18, 100);
        uint256 schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
        schnibblesTotal = uint256(
            PRBMath.mulDiv(int256(schnibblesTotal), 1e18 + finalBonusScaled, 1e18)
        );

        // ... (remaining code)
    }
}
```
Implement a minimum schnibble increment to prevent exploitation of small rounding errors:
```solidity
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
    // ... (earlier code)

    for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
        // ... (other calculations)

        uint256 newSchnibbles = uint256(
            (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
                (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
        );
        
        if (newSchnibbles - schnibblesTotal < MIN_SCHNIBBLE_INCREMENT) {
            newSchnibbles = schnibblesTotal + MIN_SCHNIBBLE_INCREMENT;
        }
        
        schnibblesTotal = newSchnibbles;

        // ... (remaining code)
    }
}
```
These changes will significantly reduce the impact of precision loss in the schnibble calculations, ensuring fairer distribution and preventing potential exploitation of rounding errors.


## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol?plain=1#L344-L345


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If the USD value of the locked tokens decreases or landlord withdraws funds, it will lower the lockWeightValueUSD, which in turn reduces the numOfPlots. This can cause legitimate users who have staked their Munchables on a landlord's plot to fail the condition `if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId)`, resulting in their toilerState being set to true and preventing them from farming their staked Munchables. 

## Proof of Concept
This is the function used to calculate numOfPlots
```js
function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
        return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    }
```

And each time the `_farmPlots` function is call this condition is check

```js
if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```
We can imagine that any minor change in LockedWeightedValue can change the numOfPlots, especially due to rounding during division. For example, if a user staked their pet on plot 40 of a landlord and, next time they want to farm, _getNumPlots returns 39, their pet will be set to dirty, preventing the user from farming it further.


## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement a validation mechanism that ensures users' staked positions remain valid even if numOfPlots changes slightly.

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol?plain=1#L272


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The lack of bounds checking on the `REALM_BONUSES` array can lead to out-of-bounds errors, causing the following potential issues:

1. **Runtime Exceptions**: If the calculated index exceeds the array length, it may cause a runtime exception, leading to the transaction being reverted.

2. **Disrupted Farming Calculations**: The farming calculations rely on the `REALM_BONUSES` array for determining bonuses. If the array access fails due to an out-of-bounds error, users will be unable to farm their staked Munchables.





## Proof of Concept

The REALM_BONUSES array is stored in a central configuration storage, and its size is dynamic. This means the array can have varying lengths, and there is no inherent guarantee about its minimum size at any given point. Proper bounds checking is crucial to avoid accessing invalid indices.

**Index Calculation** 

The index for accessing the `REALM_BONUSES` array is calculated as `(uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) + uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm) `

Consider the following enum definitions:

```js
enum Realm {
    Everfrost, // 0
    Drench,    // 1
    Moltania,  // 2
    Arridia,   // 3
    Verdentis, // 4
    Invalid    // 5
}
```

Both `immutableAttributes.realm` and `landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm` use this enum, so they can have values from 0 to 5.

Given that both enum values can range from 0 to 5, the maximum possible index calculation would be `(uint256(5) * 5) + uint256(5) = 25 + 5 = 30` 

To avoid out-of-bounds errors, the REALM_BONUSES array must contain at least 31 elements, as the code assumes the length is correctly set and does not perform any length checks before accessing indices

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To mitigate the risk of out-of-bounds errors due to insufficient length in the REALM_BONUSES array, consider checking the calculated index against the array length before performing any access.




## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L285


# Vulnerability details

## Overview
The addition of ```finalBonus``` in LOC-285 in the ```_farmPlots(address _sender)``` function is wrong.

## Proof of Concept
The ```_farmPlots(address _sender)``` function has the following calculation:

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L285

```solidity
            schnibblesTotal =
                (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
            schnibblesTotal = uint256(
                (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
            );
```

However, if we unfold the above equation, we find:

```
schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;

schnibblesTotal = uint256[{int256(schnibblesTotal) + (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)} / 100];
```

This is wrong. The purpose of the ```finalBonus``` is to increase (or decrease) the ```schnibblesTotal``` based on if it is +ve or -ve. This should be done as:

```
schnibblesTotal = uint256[{int256(schnibblesTotal) + ((int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100)}];
```

For example, with:

```
schnibblesTotal = 30 * 24 * 3600 * 0.001; (basically, 30 days (in sec) multiplied with BSR)
finalBonus = 10;
```

By the present calculation:

```
schnibblesTotal would be 285;
```

By the correct calculation:

```
schnibblesTotal would be 2851;
```

Hence, by the present calculation, stakers and landlords would lose a lot of harvest schnibbles rewards.

## Severity
Impact: The stakers and landlords lose reward value due to a wrong calculation. So, the impact is High.

Likelihood: This would happen every time a user would farm their plot. So, the likelihood is High.

Therefore, the severity is High.

## Tools Used
VS Code
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change the calculation as follows:

```diff
            schnibblesTotal =
                (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
-           schnibblesTotal = uint256(
-               (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
-                   (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100
-           );
+          schnibblesTotal = uint256(
+              (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
+                  ((int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100))
+          );

```


## Assessed type

Math

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L345

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The uint256 `PRICE_PER_PLOT` variable can be found in 3 places of the `LandManager` contract. The first one is on the 16th line where it is declared:
```solidity
uint256 PRICE_PER_PLOT;
```
The second is on the 77th line where it is set to a value retrieved from the `ConfigStorage` contract:
```solidity
PRICE_PER_PLOT = IConfigStorage(configStorage).getUint(
            StorageKey.NFTOverlord
        );
```
and the third is on the 347th line where it is used for calculation:
```solidity
function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
        return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    }
```
After a short review of the `ConfigStorage` contract and a query to the documentation bot called `Docs Wolf`, I came to the conclusion that nowhere is it checked whether `PRICE_PER_PLOT` has a value equal to 0. Thus, every function that uses `_getNumPlots` to calculate the available plots could revert due to division by zero.
## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Create a check method that ensures the value of `PRICE_PER_PLOT` is not zero, and if it is, revert with an error.

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L140


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can stake more than the intended maximum of 10 NFTs potentially gaining additional rewards or benefits that were not intended by the system's design. Additionally, It may lead to unexpected behavior if other parts of the system assume a maximum of 10 staked NFTs per Account.

## Proof of Concept
The current implementation of the `stakeMunchable` function includes a check to enforce a maximum limit of 10 staked NFTs per account. The condition used to enforce this limit is:
```
if (munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length > 10) revert TooManyStakedMunchiesError();

```
However, this condition only reverts when the number of staked NFTs exceeds 10, meaning an account can stake exactly 11 NFTs without triggering the error. This bypass occurs because the condition checks for > (greater than) rather than >= (greater than or equal to).

If for example an account with 10 staked NFTs calls the stake function, it won't revert and will proceed to stake an additional NFT

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To correctly enforce the intended limit of 10 NFTs per account, the condition should be updated to:
```
if (munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length >= 10) revert TooManyStakedMunchiesError();
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
 Users end up staking under less favorable conditions than they intended potentially leading to financial losses

## Proof of Concept
The `updateTaxRate` function allows landlords to instantly modify their tax rates `(currentTaxRate)` without any cooldown period or pending state. Concurrently, the `stakeMunchable` function processes staking actions using the `currentTaxRate` at the `time of execution`. This creates a time-of-check to time-of-use  issue where the tax rate a user bases their staking decision on may differ from the rate applied when their transaction is processed.

The underlying race condition persists due to potential delays between transaction submission and execution which can be influenced by network latency, block times and the validator's transaction ordering mechanism. This non-atomic operation in a concurrent environment creates a window of opportunity for rate changes that could be exploited by strategic landlords or lead to unintended economic outcomes for stakers.

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Allow users to lock in a rate for a certain period when they initiate a stake transaction.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L50


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
1.  All tax rates and the price per plot could be set to zero, fundamentally breaking the economic model of the system.
2.  With MIN_TAX_RATE and MAX_TAX_RATE potentially set to zero, the updateTaxRate() function's checks become meaningless allowing any tax rate to be set.
3.  If PRICE_PER_PLOT is zero, users might be able to acquire land for free leading to economic imbalance and potential system abuse.
4.  Zero-value BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE could disrupt any reward or incentive mechanisms based on this rate.

## Proof of Concept
In the `LandManager` contract's `_reconfigure()` function, critical parameters such as `MIN_TAX_RATE`, `MAX_TAX_RATE`, `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE`, `BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE`, and `PRICE_PER_PLOT ` are being initialized using incorrect storage keys. Instead of using keys specific to these parameters, the function is using keys that appear to be related to other contract addresses or unrelated configurations


These keys `(LockManager, AccountManager, ClaimManager, MigrationManager)` are likely meant for retrieving contract addresses not numerical values for tax rates and prices. Moreover, the getUint() function does not revert on non-existent keys but returns zero. This means that if these incorrect keys don't exist in the configuration (which is likely), all these critical parameters will be silently initialized to zero.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
1. Use the correct keys for each parameter ensuring they match the keys used when setting these values in the configuration contract.
2. Implement checks in the `_reconfigure` function to ensure that retrieved values are non-zero and within expected ranges: i.e
```
MIN_TAX_RATE = configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MinTaxRate);
require(MIN_TAX_RATE > 0, "MIN_TAX_RATE not set");

MAX_TAX_RATE = configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxTaxRate);
require(MAX_TAX_RATE > MIN_TAX_RATE, "Invalid MAX_TAX_RATE");

//similar for the other two values.

```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If the `landlord` unstakes their money from `lockManager` and their plots are marked as dirty, the `landlord` will not be able to receive rewards for a new plotId that becomes available when they stake money again.
A user who stakes a `MunchNFT` on the landlord's plotId could potentially never unstake it, preventing the `landlord` from receiving rewards.
In that case, the user can grief the landlord until he unstake the corresponding MunchNFT.

## Proof of Concept
- The `landlord` stakes money in `lockManager` for 10 plots, i.e. `_getNumPlots(landlord) returns 10`
- Users occupy all of the landlord's plots.
- The `landlord` unstakes part or all tokens for a short period.
- During this period, if a user performs any action with munchNFT, the internal `_farmPlots()` function marks the `landlord`'s plots as dirty.
- The `landlord` stakes part or all tokens back in `lockManager`.
- Now `_getNumPlots(landlord) returns 10` again.
- However, not all users unstake munchNFTs from the `dirty` plots of the `landlord`.
- The `landlord`'s plot IDs will remain marked as `dirty` until the user unstakes the NFT.

Dirty toilers will always be `skipped`, even if `_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId` is false:
```solidity
    timestamp = block.timestamp;
    tokenId = staked[i];
    _toiler = toilerState[tokenId];
@>  if (_toiler.dirty) continue;
    landlord = _toiler.landlord;
    if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
        timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
        // @audit if toiler is marked dirty it can't be marked as clean again, 
        toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
    }
```

The `dirty` flag changes to `false` only in `unstakeMunchable()`:

```solidity
    toilerState[tokenId] = ToilerState({
        lastToilDate: 0,
        plotId: 0,
        landlord: address(0),
        latestTaxRate: 0,
@>      dirty: false
    });
```
## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement a system that tracks the occupied time, so when the `landlord` stakes tokens again, their occupied time begins to increase again.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L283-L286


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Due to an incorrect calculation of total Schnibbles in farming plots, both toilers and landlords will harvest significantly fewer Schnibbles than anticipated. This discrepancy may adversely impact the growth of Munchables and the overall game strategy.

## Proof of Concept

In the `_farmPlots()` function, `schnibblesTotal` is calculated as follows:

```solidity
    function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
        ... ...
        for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
            ... ...
            schnibblesTotal =
                (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
            schnibblesTotal = uint256(
                (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
                    (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100 
            );
            ... ...
        }
        ... ...
    }
```

If we rewrite the above statement as formula:
$$
\text{schnibblesTotal} = \frac{(\text{schnibblesTotal} + \text{schnibblesTotal} \times \text{finalBonus})}{100}
$$

If we assume that `finalBonus` is 10%, `schnibblesTotal` is reduced to only 11% of its value. Therefore, the tailor and his landlord will receive much less Schnibbles.

I am sure the intended formula of the above statement is like the below:

$$
\text{schnibblesTotal} = \text{schnibblesTotal} + \frac{\text{schnibblesTotal} \times \text{finalBonus}}{100}
$$

I would suggest changing the issued statement as follow:

```solidity
    function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
        ... ...
        for (uint8 i = 0; i < staked.length; i++) {
            ... ...
-           schnibblesTotal = uint256(
-               (int256(schnibblesTotal) +
-                   (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus)) / 100 
-           );

+           schnibblesTotal = uint256(
+               int256(schnibblesTotal) +
+                   (int256(schnibblesTotal) * finalBonus) / 100 
+           );
            ... ...
        }
        ... ...
    }
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

As AccountManager.addSubAccount() can arbitrarily overwrite anyone’s main account, an attacker can prevent a chosen victim from unstaking their staked MunchNFT, resulting in the NFT being stuck in the contract forever.

## Proof of Concept

Consider the following scenario:

1. Assume Alice has registered her account usually via `AccountManager.register()`
2. Alice successfully stakes her NFT (`tokenId = 1`) via `LandManager.stakeMunchable()`. Note that at this point, `mainAccount = alice`. The token will be transferred to the LandManager contract and the contract’s `munchableOwner[1]` will be set to Alice.
3. Bob calls `AccountManager.addSubAccount(alice)` which sets `AccountManager`'s `mainAccounts[alice]` to Bob’s address.
4. Alice wants to unstake her token but her `LandManager.unstakeMunchable(1)` call will revert due to `InvalidOwnerError`. This is because `mainAccount` is now set to Bob’s address, so `munchableOwner[1]` does not equal to `mainAccount`. Alice will never be able to unstake her token, resulting in loss of funds.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

The AccountManager logic must be reworked to ensure that no authorized party can arbitrarily modify someone’s main account address. The simplest fix would be to remove the entire concept of subaccount. If that’s not feasible, one potential mitigation is to require an approval signature from the original main account’s address in order to override the original main account address.

It is also critical for the LandManager contract to ensure that unstaking can be performed by the original staker even if the main account changed to prevent the token from being stuck in the contract forever. One potential mitigation is to keep track of the original staker’s address for each token and in the unstaking function, it should always allow the original staker to withdraw their tokens. In such a case, it is also important that farmed schnibbles are properly calculated for the original staker as well.





## Assessed type

Access Control

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

## Proof of Concept

In `LandManager._farmPlots()`, the following snippet handles cases where the plot id doesn’t fit in the current plot metadata.

```solidity
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

However, this logic is incorrect because when `_getNumPlots(landlord) == _toiler.plotId`, it’s not marked dirty even though it should be. 

As the plot id is an index while _getNumPlots returns the size, when `_getNumPlots(landlord) == _toiler.plotId`, such a plot id does not fit in the metadata. But because the current code leaves such a plot out of this if-clause, `dirty` and `timestamp = block.timestamp` would remain unchanged, which results in more amount of farmed schnibbles than expected for this plot.

```solidity
            schnibblesTotal =

                BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
There are cases in which users munchables can be stuck inside a plot for an undefined amount of time due to lack of precautions in `LandManager::_farmPlots`

## Proof of Concept
When a user tries to unstake their Munchables the modifier `forceFarmPlots` automatically calls `_farmPlots` in order to ensure the user gets all the rewards they are entitled to. Inside the function there is an edge case stated by the developers where a landlord has unlocked some of his funds and as a result owns less plots and and plot which the user is trying to farm doesn't exist anymore. In that situation the following changes are made.

```solidity
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
@>              timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

The important part is that the timestamp is set to some time in the past (the last time the land owner updated their `currentTaxRate`). The issue lies in this calculation:

```solidity
...
            schnibblesTotal =
@>              (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
                BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
...
```

There is no guarantee that `_toiler.lastToildDate` is smaller than `timestamp` quite the opposite it is very likely that is the case if the landlord has withdrawn funds and we are in the said situation. Because of that this would force a revert to happen as `schnibblesTotal` is of type uint256 and the compiler version is 0.8.25 which reverts on underflow. Because of that the whole transaction which tries to unstake the munchables will revert and the users will not be able to get their munchables back until the landlord updates their `currentTaxRate` making `timestamp > _toiler.lastToilDate` and allowing the transaction to continue

## Tools Used

Manual review
VS Code

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Find another way to handle the edge case where the landlord has withdrawn funds from their lock.

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L259
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L281


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

A timestamp earlier than `lastToilDate` will cause the entire `_farmPlots` function to revert.

## Vulnerability Details

In the `_farmPlots()` function, the total schnibbles for each stake are calculated unsafely within a loop using the following method:

```solidity
schnibblesTotal = (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) * BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
```

The operation `(timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate)` is performed without verifying that `timestamp > _toiler.lastToilDate`. If `_getNumPlots(landlord)` is less than `_toiler.plotId`, the timestamp is set to the landlord's `lastUpdated` value:

```solidity
if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
    timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
    toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
}
```

This scenario can lead to an underflow error if a user stakes on a landlord's plot where `lastUpdated` has not been refreshed. If the landlord's `lastUpdated` remains outdated and `_getNumPlots(landlord)` becomes less than `_toiler.plotId` due to price changes or intentional unlocking actions by the landlord, the user will be unable to perform any critical actions. This is because most actions call `_farmPlots` first. A malicious landlord could exploit this by intentionally not updating `lastUpdated`, effectively causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for the renter's entire operations.

## Recommendation

Ensure that `timestamp > _toiler.lastToilDate` before performing the arithmetic operation. If this condition is not met, set `schnibblesTotal` to 0.


## Assessed type

DoS
